items.title: Industrie : des coûts en hausse et un emploi qui fléchit
items.description: Les industriels dressent un tableau contrasté du troisième trimestre 2026 : un climat des affaires jugé globalement normal, mais des coûts de production en progression générale et des perspectives d’emploi orientées à la baisse pour la fin d’année, d’après les résultats de l’enquête de conjoncture de Bank Al-Maghrib. Le climat général des affaires a été qualifié de « normal » par 69% des industriels interrogés, tandis que 22% l’ont jugé « défavorable ». Les nuances sont sensibles d’une branche à l’autre. La part des avis défavorables atteint 27% dans le textile et cuir, 25% dans l’agroalimentaire et 19% dans la chimie et parachimie. La mécanique et métallurgie se démarque : 60% de ses entreprises parlent d’un climat normal et 27% d’un climat favorable. Côté production, l’approvisionnement en matières premières a été jugé normal par 81% des entreprises et difficile par 17%. La mécanique et métallurgie affiche les conditions les plus confortables, avec 90% d’avis « normal » contre 6% de « difficile ». La chimie et parachimie suit avec 88% et 12%, devant le textile et cuir (75% et 25%). L’agroalimentaire est la branche la plus exposée : 62% des entreprises évoquent un approvisionnement normal, mais 36% le qualifient de difficile. Parmi les principaux freins au développement de la production, les entreprises citent l’insuffisance de la demande, le niveau élevé des coûts des intrants et l’accentuation de la concurrence, singulièrement celle du secteur informel. Les coûts unitaires de production, eux, ont augmenté dans toutes les branches d’activité. Pour l’ensemble de l’industrie, 57% des entreprises font état d’une hausse, 40% d’une stagnation et seulement 3% d’une baisse. Sur le front de l’emploi, les effectifs ont stagné selon 64% des industriels et reculé selon 22%. La mécanique et métallurgie (83% de stagnation, 13% de baisse) et le textile et cuir (78% et 19%) restent proches de la stabilité, alors que la chimie et parachimie voit 31% de ses entreprises signaler une réduction, contre 60% de stagnation. L’agroalimentaire fait exception, avec 33% d’entreprises qui déclarent des embauches et 64% une stabilité. Pour le quatrième trimestre de 2026, les chefs d’entreprise anticipent globalement une baisse des effectifs, et ce dans toutes les branches. La situation de trésorerie a été jugée normale par 84% des entreprises et difficile par 14% d’entre elles. Les tensions sont plus marquées dans le textile et cuir (81% de « normale », 19% de « difficile »), la mécanique et métallurgie (86% et 14%) et l’agroalimentaire (75% et 22%). Les industriels de la chimie et parachimie décrivent, pour leur part, une trésorerie globalement normale. L’accès au financement bancaire a été considéré comme normal par les entreprises, notamment dans la mécanique et métallurgie et dans la chimie et parachimie. Les professionnels de l’agroalimentaire l’estiment toutefois difficile, alors que ceux du textile et cuir le jugent facile. Le coût du crédit est resté stable pour 90% des entreprises, contre 9% qui constatent une hausse. Cette dernière pèse davantage dans la mécanique et métallurgie, où 26% des entreprises la signalent, et dans le textile et cuir (10%). La majorité des entreprises de l’agroalimentaire et de la chimie et parachimie font état d’un coût du crédit inchangé. Les dépenses d’investissement ont progressé, selon les industriels, dans toutes les branches à l’exception du textile et cuir, où elles auraient reculé. Elles ont été financées à hauteur de 75% par des fonds propres et de 25% par crédit. Pour les trois prochains mois, les entreprises prévoient globalement une nouvelle hausse de ces dépenses, sauf dans le textile et cuir, où une baisse est attendue. The post Industrie : des coûts en hausse et un emploi qui fléchit appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Nollywood actor Diewait Ikpechukwu dies at 71
items.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Diewait Ikpechukwu has died at the age of 71, bringing to an end a career that spanned more than two decades in the Nigerian film industry. The actor reportedly died on Thursday, November 5, 2026, with the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN) confirming his passing on Friday, November 6. AGN National President, Alhaji Abubakar Sanusi Yakubu, announced the death in a tribute, describing Ikpechukwu as another legend whose memories would remain with the industry. Ikpechukwu was particularly recognised for his portrayal of traditional rulers and other authoritative characters in Nollywood productions. His performances in films such as Evil Men , alongside veteran actor Pete Edochie, as well as Python King , The Guilty and Omera , earned him recognition among audiences. Beyond his work on screen, he played an active role in the Actors Guild of Nigeria, serving as chairman of its Enugu State chapter, where he supported and mentored emerging actors. His journey into entertainment, however, was not limited to acting. Before establishing himself in Nollywood, Ikpechukwu was an accomplished footballer in the 1970s and reportedly earned an invitation to join Nigeria’s national team, then known as the Green Eagles. He later ventured into radio broadcasting, working as a sports commentator before pursuing a career in film. Ikpechukwu is survived by his wife, Gloria, children and grandchildren, who join colleagues, friends and fans in mourning his passing. His death marks another loss for Nollywood, particularly among the generation of actors whose performances helped shape the Nigerian film industry.

items.title: Mining Reforms Must Protect Jobs, Investment and Community Interests — Ghana Chamber of Mines
items.description: The Ghana Chamber of Mines has called for sustained dialogue and careful consideration of the economic implications of ongoing mining sector reforms, stressing that efforts to deepen Ghanaian participation must also safeguard employment, investment and the industry’s long-term competitiveness. The Chamber’s Chief Operating Officer, Ahmed Dasana Nantogmah, said recent concerns expressed by mineworkers and host communities highlighted the importance of consultation and a balanced approach to mining policy and regulatory decisions. His comments follow protests by mineworkers at Akyem Abirem over the directive to transition certain mining operations from owner mining to contract mining. The workers have raised concerns about potential implications for job security, wages, benefits and existing conditions of service. Mr. Nantogmah acknowledged government’s commitment to strengthening local participation in the mining industry, describing it as an important national objective that the Chamber supports. “Greater Ghanaian participation in mining is an objective we all share. However, the approach must protect existing jobs, maintain safety and operational efficiency, and ensure that the industry remains competitive enough to sustain investment and create new opportunities,” he said. He emphasised that significant changes to established mining operating models require meaningful consultation among regulators, mining companies, employees and other stakeholders to ensure that policy objectives are achieved without unintended economic consequences. Commenting on the ongoing discussions surrounding the renewal of Gold Fields Ghana’s Tarkwa mining leases, Mr. Nantogmah acknowledged the expectations of host communities for greater and more visible benefits from mineral development. “Mining communities must see tangible improvements in their livelihoods. Equally, investors must have confidence that their rights and obligations will be administered fairly and consistently. These objectives are not mutually exclusive,” he stated. He stressed the importance of constructive engagement with traditional authorities and other stakeholders, while ensuring that decisions concerning mineral rights are guided by transparent, predictable and lawful procedures. Mr. Nantogmah also noted the recent regulatory developments involving Adamus Resources and Northern Ashanti Mines, emphasising the importance of continued engagement in addressing such matters. He acknowledged the responsibility of the Minerals Commission and the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources to ensure compliance with mining laws, while encouraging dialogue, due process and mutual understanding in resolving regulatory concerns in the interest of sustaining investor confidence and protecting Ghana’s mining industry. The COO further pointed to recent operational and financial results announced by Galiano Gold and AngloGold Ashanti as indications of the industry’s capacity to sustain production and pursue further investment opportunities. He noted that realising this potential requires a stable operating environment, access to capital and a competitive fiscal and regulatory framework. “Our collective objective should be to develop mining policies that secure fair revenues for the State, expand opportunities for Ghanaian businesses, protect jobs and deliver lasting benefits to communities, while encouraging the investments needed to sustain future mineral production,” he said. Mr. Nantogmah reaffirmed the Chamber’s commitment to working constructively with government, regulators, organised labour, traditional authorities and other stakeholders to strengthen Ghana’s position as a competitive and responsible mining investment destination.

items.title: The Education a STEM Major Needs
items.description: This is an edition of the Books Briefing, our editors’ weekly guide to the best in books. Sign up for it here. In 2014, I graduated from college with a dubious degree: I majored in English, a discipline that, in a time of growing STEM mania, was widely considered a relic of questionable value. At the end of my studies, my adviser asked me what I’d taken away from the program. My answer: how to think. I had spent enough time examining the minds of brilliant others—learning how they chose words, built characters, and developed ideas—to feel some mastery over my own. In a new Atlantic essay , Joshua Bennett, a literature professor at MIT, makes the case that such an education should be foundational for all students, including and perhaps especially those focusing on science. First, here are six new stories from The Atlantic ’s Books section: Six books you should read twice He was hugely influential. He also had a foolish streak. Forget grit. The golden age of hockey literature What if the apocalypse is already here? “The Toll,” a poem by Forrest Gander Bennett’s students have grown up in a society defined by rapid technological growth; some of them likely dream of building a world we can’t imagine today, especially now that new AI technologies are pushing the frontier of the possible. At the same time, the state of the humanities has become even more fragile than it was during my undergraduate career. Humanities departments across the country are being squeezed or shut down entirely. Too many students have never been assigned the once-standard task of reading a whole book. The number of undergraduate humanities degrees awarded by American universities in 2025 was nearly a third lower than it was in 2012, although the decline might be approaching a plateau. That crisis is part of what’s driving Bennett and some of his colleagues to design a Great Books course for MIT, the kind of sweeping introduction to canonical, time-tested literature and philosophy that helps anchor many liberal-arts educations. Given the students he’s working with, Bennett’s program will focus on “the history, poetics, and philosophy of science.” A solid grounding in the humanities, he argues, is essential to the intellectual development of future scientists, in part because it can help them “identify irreplaceable ideas during a time of accelerated change.” The possibility of an imminent techno-utopia, in which work is automated and life is easy—or, conversely, a tech-driven apocalypse, in which human inventions come to subjugate humanity—makes it ever more important to teach students how to engage deeply with the age-old query: What is life for? Studying the plays of the ancient Greeks or the logical puzzles of Kant won’t, of course, provide a single answer. But doing so can help teach students how to think about the problem—to wonder, What is the meaning of life? as well as, What distinguishes a thoughtful idea from a shallow truism? To ask more questions, and to pursue the answers with rigor, is to open more routes toward meaning. Bennett’s “irreplaceable ideas” are not formulas to memorize; they’re vigorous, adaptable entities. You cannot learn, once and for all, what they mean. You can only build the habit of thinking about them for yourself. Illustration by The Atlantic . Source: Getty. The Time Is Right for a ‘Great Books’ Revival By Joshua Bennett To build a better world in the age of AI, students need grounding in indispensable ideas. Read the full article. What to Read The Perfectionists , by Simon Winchester The Perfectionists dramatically explores the history of engineers figuring out how to manufacture things—mostly out of metal, glass and other hard materials—into exacting shapes and sizes, making possible our world of cars, jet engines, and microprocessor chips. The story begins, and is intimately bound up, with the Industrial Revolution. John Wilkinson, one of the fathers of precision engineering, devised snug-fitting cylinders for James Watt’s steam engine, and the early days of the discipline are similarly full of delightfully specific historical objects: pulleys made for British naval ships, for example, and the fiddly bits of flintlock muskets. But as Winchester steps through the great advancements that pushed this school of engineering to new extremes, he makes clear that we now rely on machines to achieve a perfection unattainable by people, and that this comes with hefty stakes. An improperly machined oil pipe, for instance, caused catastrophic engine failure on a 2010 Qantas flight because it was “about half a millimeter too thin,” he writes. (Thanks to an experienced crew, everyone on board survived.) Perhaps, he suggests, a deeper respect for imperfect human craftsmanship might live alongside our reverence for mechanical technique. — Chelsea Leu From our list: Eight books that explain how the world works Out Next Week 📚 The Land of Tears and Hope: The Ukrainian Story , by Illia Ponomarenko 📚 Vocal Break: On Women, Music, and Power , by Lauren Elkin 📚 No Such Thing as Monday: A Novel , by Siân Hughes Your Weekend Read Ian Loring Shiver and Minnie Park for The Atlantic The Rise of the Tallboy Is a Sign of the Times By Megan Garber Say you’re at a football game (fun!), in large part for the food (correct!). You have spent your time at the stadium successfully curating an alfresco fine-dining experience: the pregame amuse-bouche (popcorn, maybe, with a swirl of let’s-agree-to-call-it-butter), the first-quarter aperitif (a frosty can of beer), the second-quarter appetizer (a plate of fries, doused with ketchup), the third-quarter entrée (nachos, obviously, washed down with a second beer). It’s now the fourth quarter, and although the game has gone as planned (probably? you haven’t been paying tons of attention), your dessert course has not. The menu options before you—churro, cotton candy—are leaving you stymied. That is possibly because, you come to realize, you are unexpectedly drunk. Read the full article. items.title: Petrol price down by Rs6.59 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs4.25 in fifth straight reduction
items.description: The government on Friday once again decreased the price of petrol by Rs6.59 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.25, in the fifth consecutive cut in fuel prices. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs346 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs378. The prices are applicable from Nov 7 (Saturday) to Nov 10 (Tuesday) due to a public holiday on Nov 9, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end. Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). Rise in fuel prices The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months. On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: COCOBOD relaunches free fertilizer programme with new monitoring platform to boost farmer incomes
items.description: The government has relaunched the Free Fertilizer and Agro-Input Programme for cocoa farmers under a major intervention to restore productivity, improve farmer incomes, and reset the cocoa sector. The program is a policy shift from a 50-per cent subsidy to free fertilizer distribution to farmers, which the Ghana Cocoa Board says represents a total reset of how government intends to support farmers and increase cocoa production. The relaunch of the program has seen the procurement of over 3.5 million bags of granular fertilizer for distribution to cocoa farmers nationwide. Approximately 1.2 million bags have already been delivered to farmers as a new digital platform has been developed to strengthen accountability and ensure fair distribution. Speaking at the event, Chief Executive Officer of COCOBOD, Dr. Randy Abbey, described the intervention as a decisive declaration that government, through COCOBOD, is fully committed to relieving the financial burdens of farmers. He explained the initiative also seeks to restore maximum productivity to the soil and secure the golden future of the cocoa sector. “We are removing financial barriers to high yields. Free fertilizer is not a handout; it is an investment in farmers, in the soil, and in the foreign exchange earnings of this republic,” Dr. Abbey said. The relaunch held at Sefwi Wiawso under the theme: “ Cocoa Sector Reset: Free Fertilizer for Increased Productivity and Improved Farmer Income ,” brought together government officials, traditional leaders, farmers, and other stakeholders in the cocoa value chain. Farmers with mature and productive cocoa plantations in designated operational district areas are expected to receive fertilizer, whether granular or liquid, as well as insecticides and fungicides. The COCOBOD will also supply free pneumatic and motorized sprayers to farmers. Dr. Abbey noted that the board is fully aware of the challenges that plagued previous free distribution systems, highlighting that the good intentions of the state to revamp the sector were rather undermined by diversion, smuggling, favouritism, and unfair distribution. “Inputs meant for genuine farmers ended up in open markets across the borders and on the farms of the well-connected, while smallholder farmers at the end of the line went home empty-handed,” he noted. The COCOBOD is rolling out a new digital system to track every input taken from the warehouses to farms to ensure accountability and prevent abuse of the reintroduced initiative. According to the COCOBOD boss, every beneficiary must register and have their farms marked and captured on the Digital Cocoa Management System (CMS). The identity of every farmer will be verified at the point of collection through the national identification card or by biometric data. “This time, we have built the entire distribution around a new digital distribution system that follows every bag or litre of input from the warehouse to the farm. No one can collect the fertilizer and the agro-inputs in another person’s name, and no ghost farmer names can appear on the list,” Dr. Abbey said. He added that the system calculates each farmer’s entitlement automatically based on the marked size and condition of the farm, and therefore, officers at distribution points cannot add or deduct from the allocation. Dr. Abbey cautioned smugglers and saboteurs, stressing that any officer, buyer, or individual found diverting or selling the distribution inputs will face the full rigours of the law. The cocoa industry continues to face significant challenges, including declining productivity, ageing and unproductive farms, rising production costs, labour constraints, soil fertility challenges, persistent threats of capsid pests and swollen shoot virus disease, and the increasing effects of climate variability. Highlighting the importance of cocoa to the country’s economy, Board Chairman of the COCOBOD, Dr. Samuel Ofosu-Ampofo, noted that these challenges require deliberate, coordinated and sustained interventions. He noted that the distribution of the fertilizers is in line with the government’s commitment to addressing the challenges confronting the cocoa value chain. “We cannot expect increased national cocoa production without investing adequately in the farms and supporting the farmers who cultivate them. Equally, we cannot achieve sustainable productivity if we do not address the underlying challenges of soil fertility, pest and disease management, access to improved planting material and effective extension services,” he said. Additionally, the COCOBOD says 1.8 million litres of liquid fertilizer, 2.3 million litres of insecticide, and 1.5 million kilograms of fungicide have been purchased for cocoa farmers across the country. Dr. Ofosu-Ampofo said that the government has unprecedentedly supplied about 27,000 new spray machines in a single year, bringing the total number of spray machines available to about 67,000. To complement the supply of sprayers and chemicals, he also noted that approximately 5.7 million litres of pre-mixed fuel have been supplied to cocoa farmers to support the mechanical application of liquid fertilizer and insecticides. The board and management of COCOBOD say they remain committed to ensuring a sustainable cocoa economy that provides optimal benefits to farmers, sustains profitable and integrated value chains, as well as promotes environmental resilience and social inclusion.

items.title: Military force alone cannot defeat terrorism – Buratai
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Former Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Tukur Buratai (retd.), has said that military force alone cannot defeat terrorism in Nigeria, stressing the need to address poverty, unemployment, poor governance and other socio-economic factors fuelling insecurity. Buratai, who spoke on Friday in Lagos at the public presentation of a book, Beyond Military Force: A Strategy for Countering Terrorism in Nigeria, said although military operations remained essential in confronting armed groups, sustainable peace could only be achieved through a combination of military and non-military interventions. The former army chief, who served between 2015 and 2021, described the book as an important intellectual contribution to Nigeria’s counter-terrorism efforts, noting that security challenges in the North-East and North-West required a comprehensive strategy beyond the use of weapons. “Military force, however professional, is a shield, not a substitute for governance. It can create the conditions for peace, but it cannot by itself build peace. “It can degrade a terrorist group; it cannot alone remove the grievances of poverty, ignorance and manipulation from which such groups recruit,” he said. Buratai emphasised the importance of intelligence gathering and community participation in counter-insurgency operations, describing local communities as indispensable partners in the fight against terrorism. According to him, security agencies cannot achieve meaningful results without the confidence and cooperation of the communities they are deployed to protect. “No amount of firepower can compensate for poor intelligence. The community is often the best source of intelligence, but only when the community trusts the security agencies,” he stated. He also warned that human rights violations during military operations could alienate local communities and provide terrorist organisations with propaganda materials to attract new recruits. Buratai disclosed that the Nigerian Army reviewed its rules of engagement during his tenure to ensure compliance with prevailing standards, while introducing human rights desks and other accountability mechanisms. He called for stronger counter-terrorism capacity within the Nigeria Police Force, arguing that the military should not continue to shoulder responsibilities traditionally assigned to civilian security institutions. “The military is not the police; it is not the social welfare agency; it is not the school system. When the military is deployed to perform tasks that belong to civil authorities, it becomes overstretched, and the roots of the conflict remain untouched,” he said. On the rehabilitation and reintegration of former terrorists, the retired general supported credible deradicalisation programmes but insisted that such initiatives must not undermine justice for victims of terrorism. He said rehabilitation efforts must be transparent, properly monitored and community-based, adding that affected communities needed assurances that justice had been served. Drawing from his experience as commander of the Multinational Joint Task Force headquartered in N’Djamena, Chad, Buratai advocated stronger regional security cooperation, noting that terrorist organisations, including Boko Haram and its affiliates, operated across national boundaries. He urged Nigeria to strengthen collaboration with neighbouring countries and regional institutions, including the Economic Community of West African States, African Union and countries within the Lake Chad Basin. The former army chief also supported the recommendation for a state of emergency on poverty in Northern Nigeria, saying the initiative should prioritise out-of-school children, the Almajiri system, youth unemployment, vocational training and social protection. He, however, cautioned that poverty alleviation programmes must be transparent and protected against elite capture. “Poverty is not an excuse for terrorism, but it is a fertile ground for recruitment and manipulation. We must treat it with the seriousness it deserves,” he said. Citing findings from the book, Buratai said field surveys conducted across Adamawa, Borno, Yobe, Kano, Kebbi, Kogi, Niger and the Federal Capital Territory showed that 86 per cent of respondents believed negotiation could be helpful in addressing terrorism, while 92 per cent agreed that community members could contribute significantly to intelligence gathering. He added that 84 per cent of respondents linked terrorist recruitment to poor economic conditions and the Almajiri situation. Earlier, the author, Dr. Joan Ugo Mbagwu, a Professor of Peace, Criminology and Security Studies at Chrisland University, Abeokuta, Ogun State, said the book was conceived to broaden national understanding of counter-terrorism beyond the conventional reliance on military force. Mbagwu, who disclosed that she had conducted research for the Ford Foundation and the Institute for Development Studies, also served as a Process Evaluator for the United Nations Peacebuilding Fund in Africa. The book was formally unveiled by retired Major General R.O. Yusuf, while the Chairman of the occasion, Olubunmi Ajala, commended Buratai for his commitment to security-related issues. An award of appreciation was also presented to the former army chief in recognition of his contributions to combating terrorism during his tenure. The post Military force alone cannot defeat terrorism – Buratai appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Farmers urged to enroll in insurance policies to protect investments against El Niño impacts
items.description: The recent climatic phenomenon, El Niño, is prompting the urgency for farmers to take immediate steps to seek insurance protection for their investments. Despite the rollout of insurance policies, including the Ghana Agriculture Insurance Pool, for the agricultural value chain, many farmers fail to leverage the avenues to mitigate financial hardship brought about by unpredictable weather conditions and crop diseases. The Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana is pushing for farmers to safeguard their investment now against the vagaries of the harsh weather as the world is predicted to further heat up in the ensuing years. Weather and climate experts predict intense weather conditions in the coming years, exposing uninsured farmers to more threats of loss. Despite a pool of insurance policies, farmers continue to lose out on their benefits. The insurers are moving to strengthen insurance products for the agriculture sector to rope in more farmers to safeguard their investments. Speaking at the annual conference of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana in Kumasi, Chairman of the Insurance Awareness Coordinators Group, Wilson Teye, highlighted challenges confronting the rollout and uptake of the policies by farmers. “We haven’t had mechanized agriculture. We depend completely on the vagaries of the weather and that is a problem. Even some of our methods, such as deliberately setting fires on farms, are issues. There is also the challenge of bring all the farmers together to understand and appreciate the need for insurance. But regardless, we have brought this to the forefront and are addressing agricultural insurance,” he said. Agricultural insurance provides protection to key stakeholders in the agricultural production value chain in the event of crop failure ad livestock mortality due to both natural phenomena and human-induced activities. President of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana, Solomon Nii Amah-Kai Lartey, says the time is now for vulnerable large- and small-scale farmers to secure their produce. “Make sure you have your insurance now. There is parametric insurance, which does need much assessment after a loss. Once the parameters are triggered, a claim can be made. With the emergence of El Niño, people should get insured now,” he said. Mr. Amah-Kai also disclosed that farmers and other stakeholders along the agriculture value chain can leverage the dedicated insurance pool for subsidized products. “The Ghana Agriculture Insurance Pool is available for agriculture stakeholders. This pool is there to ensure that agric insurance premiums are subsidized for people to be able to buy insurance,” he said. Deputy Commissioner of Insurance, Bernard Ohemeng Baah, emphasized the importance of insurance for agriculture as he revealed that the National Insurance Commission is in its concluding stages to roll out subsidized agriculture insurance for smallholder farmers. “Because we don’t have data, the price of insurance for farmers tends to be really high. So, many of them don’t patronize it. We are employing innovative approaches to deliver insurance to farmers at a low cost. This will help protect Ghana’s food basket and also ensure that families that depend on agriculture are not exposed to the shocks of the weather,” he said. Closing the Insurance Gap The AGM and educational conference of the insurers, held on the theme: “ Closing the Gap: From Awareness to Action in Building an Adaptive Insurance Industry ,” assembled professional stakeholders in the sector to leverage the opportunity in building a resilient insurance industry. Ghana’s insurance industry, despite making considerable gains, is still confronted with significant gaps between public awareness, insurance ownership, and effective financial protection. In 2024, Ghana’s insurance penetration stood at approximately 1.0 per cent of the gross domestic product (GDP). The International Financial Reporting Standards report 0.63 per cent associated with insurance service revenue. But insurers only paid approximately 3.6 billion cedis in claims during 2024. Mr. Nii Amah-Kai noted that the challenge must extend beyond just raising awareness but must extend insurance protection to more people and businesses and also to ensure that the experience of purchasing and using insurance justifies the public’s confidence in the insurance cover. “We need to make sure that the awareness we are creating is translating into real insurance take-up. This conference seeks to find answers to whether or not the awareness is properly done and how it is benefiting the Ghanaian people,” he said. Mr. Wilson Teye says people’s trust and confidence must be heightened to increase their enrolment in insurance policy avenues. “The bedrock of insurance is payment of claims. If people do not trust that their claims will be paid and on time, they naturally wouldn’t want their money buying insurance. The objective is to address the mistrust and get regulatory intervention,” he said. As part of the annual activities, the association also visited the T.I. Ahmadiyya SHS in Kumasi to sensitize students on the job prospects in pursuing study programmes in insurance and actuarial science. The association also invested in the digital infrastructure of the school with the donation of printers and learning projectors to aid academic work, while also providing some souvenirs from member insurance companies.

items.title: États-Unis : le nom du physicien algérien Noureddine Melikechi gravé pour l’éternité à l’Université du Massachusetts
items.description: Nouvelle consécration pour Noureddine Melikechi aux Etats-Unis. Cette fois, l’université de Massachusetts a décidé d’inscrire dans le marbre et pour l’éternité le nom du célèbre physicien et chercheur algérien. Le prestigieux réseau public d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche américain a créé un programme de financement des professeurs de cette université qui présentent des idées novatrices en matière de recherche et d’éducation, a appris TSA ce vendredi auprès de M. Melikechi. Ce programme est baptisé « Dean Noureddine Melikechi Endowed Kennedy College of Sciences Faculty Innovation Fellowships.” « L’université de Massachusetts et Monsieur Kennedy ont décidé et annoncé qu’ils créaient un programme qui portera mon nom pour l’éternité. Ce programme consiste à financer des professeurs de l’université de Massachusetts qui présentent des idées innovatrices en matière de recherche, d’éducation », explique le célèbre chercheur algérien qui vient de publier ses mémoires, « Nour. Noureddine Melikechi » , aux Éditions Barzakh en Algérie. Pour lancer ce programme, l’université du Massachusetts a consenti un investissement initial de 2.5 millions de dollars. Noureddine Melikechi : « Je ne m’attendais pas à cela, du moins de mon vivant » « C’est un très un grand honneur. Je suis heureux que la famille Kennedy et l’université de Massachusetts me font cet honneur. Avoir son nom lié à un programme pour l’éternité est quelque chose à laquelle je ne m’attendais pas, du moins pas de mon vivant », a ajouté le doyen du Kennedy College of Sciences. Diplômé en physique de l’université de Bab Ezzouar (Alger), Noureddine Melikechi a poursuivi ses études en physique à l’université de Sussex en Angleterre avant de s’installer aux Etats-Unis où il mène des travaux de recherche qui « couvrent un large éventail de domaines de la physique atomique, moléculaire et optique, avec des contributions à la spectroscopie, à l'optique non linéaire, à la détection optique, aux mesures de haute précision et à la biophotonique », précise le Kennedy College of Sciences dont il est le doyen depuis 1996. Membre de l'équipe de la mission Mars Science Laboratory de la NASA , Noureddine Melikechi fait partie du Haut conseil des scientifiques de la communauté algérienne à l’étranger. Il est l’auteur de plusieurs publications et obtenu de nombreux prix et distinctions dont le Prix d'excellence de groupe de la NASA, équipe de développement et de recherche scientifique de l'instrument ChemCam du Mars Science Laboratory, NASA en 2013 et le Prix présidentiel de recherche, Université d'État du Delaware en 1998. L’article États-Unis : le nom du physicien algérien Noureddine Melikechi gravé pour l'éternité à l'Université du Massachusetts est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 2027: ADC-PCC vows to sustain campaigns despite leadership crisis
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike Following the filing of an appeal against the Federal High Court judgment on its leadership dispute, the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council has vowed to sustain its campaigns for the 2027 elections, insisting that the crisis will not distract it from its mission or stop its mobilisation across the country. The council is determined to keep its political machinery running and its message before Nigerians, even as it battles to protect party’s leadership structure from the fallout of the November 5 judgment. In a statement on Friday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the party disclosed that it had also applied for a stay of execution of the judgment involving Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe and the ADC. It said the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, was formally notified of the appeal and stay application on November 6. The ADC urged INEC to exercise restraint and refrain from taking any consequential action on the party’s leadership while the legal challenge remained pending. Appealing to members, supporters and Nigerians, Shaibu urged them not to lose confidence in the party or its political project. “To our members, supporters and Nigerians who believe in democracy: remain calm, steadfast and confident. This is not the end of the road. The ADC is taking every lawful step to defend its rights, and we will not be intimidated or distracted from that responsibility,” he said. The campaign council insisted that the leadership dispute would not interrupt its political activities or its engagement with Nigerians. “Our campaigns continue without interruption. There is no stopping the affordability train or our mission to make life better for Nigerians. We will keep taking our message to the people as we pursue every lawful avenue to defend our rights,” Shaibu stated. The council expressed confidence that the dispute would receive a full hearing, maintaining that it would continue to pursue all lawful avenues to defend its interests. items.title: Lanala Groupe dévoile sa nouvelle identité et annonce le lancement prochain de Lanala Banque
items.description: Le groupe Lanala a présenté, ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026, à Conakry, sa nouvelle identité visuelle. Cette transformation accompagne l’évolution de ses activités et son ambition de construire un écosystème financier intégré en Guinée. À cette occasion, ses responsables ont annoncé le lancement prochain de Lanala Banque, prévu avant la fin de l’année 2026. Né en 2017 avec Lanala Assurance, le groupe Lanala franchit une nouvelle étape de son développement. Neuf ans après ses débuts dans le secteur des assurances, l’entreprise change d’identité visuelle et adopte désormais la marque Lanala Groupe. Lors de la cérémonie de présentation, la Présidente de Lanala Holding a expliqué que ce changement va au-delà d'une simple modification de logo. Il traduit, selon Dre Meniane Christelle Doré, la volonté de construire un groupe plus structuré autour de métiers complémentaires. « Ce changement ne se limite pas à un nouveau nom ou à de nouveaux logos. Il traduit la transformation de notre groupe, la diversification de nos métiers et surtout une volonté de construire une identité commune plus forte et plus cohérente », a-t-elle déclaré. Désormais, Lanala Groupe rassemble plusieurs entités : Lanala Assurance, Lanala Assurance Vie, Lanala Finance, Lanala Digital Pay, Lanala Fondation et, prochainement, Lanala Banque. Chaque filiale disposera de sa propre identité visuelle et de sa couleur, tout en conservant une appartenance commune au groupe. La directrice de communication a également présenté les fondements de cette nouvelle identité. Le nouvel emblème repose sur deux blocs de tailles différentes, qui symbolisent, selon Sophie Anne Zogbélémou, la progression, la croissance, la solidarité et la fiabilité. Elle a aussi rappelé la signification du nom Lanala, qui renvoie à la confiance dans plusieurs langues parlées en Guinée. Lanala Banque annoncée avant la fin de l'année L'une des principales annonces de cette rencontre concerne la création de Lanala Banque. Ce projet doit permettre au groupe de compléter son offre de services financiers et de contribuer à l'élargissement de la bancarisation en Guinée. Interrogé sur le calendrier de lancement, le directeur Lanala Digital Pay Tamba Zacharie Millimono a indiqué que l'ouverture est envisagée avant la fin de l'année 2026. « À la fin de cette année, Dieu voulant, la banque va être lancée. Et ça va être une banque différente, une banque unique en Guinée », a-t-il annoncé, sans donner davantage de précisions sur les produits et services qui seront proposés. Le groupe ambitionne également de rapprocher ses différentes offres des populations à travers le concept de Lanala Center. Ces futurs centres de services devraient regrouper, dans un même espace, les prestations liées aux assurances, à la microfinance, aux paiements électroniques et à la banque. « Les Guinéens, nos clients, pourront accéder à un écosystème intégré où chaque filiale est représentée, où son service et son métier sont proposés aux consommateurs », a expliqué Tamba Zacharie Millimono, représentant de Lanala Groupe. Plus de 700 emplois et un investissement dans la jeunesse Au-delà de sa transformation institutionnelle et commerciale, le groupe met également en avant son impact sur l’emploi et la formation. Selon les chiffres communiqués par ses responsables, Lanala compte 727 emplois directs et indirects. Le groupe a également lancé le programme Pépites Lanala, qui accueille 40 jeunes talents. Par ailleurs, 20 autres jeunes suivent depuis six mois une formation aux métiers bancaires en prévision de l'ouverture de la nouvelle banque. Pour la Présidente du groupe Lanala Holding, cette politique de formation et de recrutement constitue un volet important de la croissance du groupe. « Notre plus belle réussite ne sera pas seulement de bâtir des entreprises qui grandissent, mais de permettre à des femmes et à des hommes de grandir avec elles », a souligné Dre Meniane Christelle Doré.

items.title: Activists breach Microsoft data centre construction site as protests spread in Europe
items.description: Protesters broke into the construction site of a Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam on Friday at the start of two days of rallies that are part of a growing global backlash over the rapid build-out of computing power needed for AI. Activist groups have announced actions in 16 countries on Friday and Saturday, according to the “ Stop Dirty Data Centres ” coalition, which is rallying environmental groups and digital rights campaigns behind calls to pause large-scale construction. In Amsterdam on Friday, more than 100 activists gathered at the construction site of a Microsoft AI data centre, marching arm in arm before breaking into the site, climbing cranes, hanging balloons and dancing while police stood by. Some carried placards with messages reading: “Screw your data centre”. “These data centres are destroying our world. It’s becoming uninhabitable because of all the resources they consume. That’s why we’re here today,” protester Sam van der Beek said. Site owner Pure Data Centres, which plans to invest more than $1 billion and is backed by Brookfield-owned Oaktree, said it was committed to engagement with local stakeholders. “We respectfully ask those on site to leave safely and engage with us in dialogue about the development and any concerns they may have,” it said. Other planned actions include a march in Dublin, a protest outside the parliament building in Warsaw, and a demonstration against a different Microsoft data centre in Denmark. Microsoft said it understood that people had strong feelings about the project and respected their right to express them peacefully but did not condone any unlawful actions. Concern over AI drives stock market rout Pushback is growing from Spain to India and the United States, where technology stocks fell sharply on Thursday over concern that Democratic control of Congress could mean tougher regulation curtails the AI boom. Campaigners say data centres pressure electricity and water supplies, compete with housing and other businesses for scarce resources and threaten climate goals. They also point to job losses and potential risks to personal and national security from private and big tech concentrating power. Technology companies argue that data centres are essential to meeting global demand for artificial intelligence and cloud computing and provide critical infrastructure for businesses, governments and consumers. Stop Dirty Data Centres says it is not anti-progress or calling for existing data centres to be closed but that major construction should be halted until governments establish clearer rules. Europe is divided between its ambition to catch up with the US and Asia on AI to boost productivity and to maintain what are generally more stringent controls and public protections. Speaking to Reuters on Thursday, EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said Europe needed more data centres to power AI development, though she added it needed to be done with care. “AI, of course, is a super important technology and we need to have our own capacity,” Virkkunen said, pointing to investments being made in chip-making capacity, AI startups and a plan to build out gigafactories around the region. However, she added, “It’s very important for citizens that they can trust that their energy bills are not skyrocketing and there are no electricity blackouts because of data centres, or they are not destroying the environment with these projects.” A Google project in Finland faces a criminal probe over land clearances, Italy and Portugal are tightening environmental regulation for data centres, and Microsoft pulled out of a UK data centre project that was hit by infrastructure delays. The Netherlands has about 200 data centres either planned, under construction or in operation.

items.title: District Health Information Management System fully restored – Health Ministry
items.description: The Ministry of Health says the District Health Information Management System (DHIMS) has been successfully restored and is now fully operational following a temporary disruption. In a press release issued on November 6, 2026, the Ministry said the system, which is managed by the Ghana Health Service (GHS), supports the collation and management of health information at the district level. The Ministry expressed appreciation to stakeholders for their patience and understanding during the period of disruption. It, however, clarified that the Ghana Health Information Management System (GHIMS), used by hospitals to manage patient and medical records, was not affected by the disruption and remained operational throughout the period. The clarification is expected to address concerns about the potential impact of the disruption on hospital operations and the management of patients’ medical records. The Ministry reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening digital health systems to improve efficiency, data management and healthcare delivery across the country. Read also: Afenyo-Markin pushes for Health Minister’s appearance over shutdown of health information systems over $64m debt Earlier, Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin was pushing for the Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, to appear before the House to explain the shutdown of the system. items.title: Sheikh Umar Ibrahim Imam removed as National Imam of ASWAJ
items.description: The National Da’awa Council (NADAC) of the Ahlussunna Wal Jama’a (ASWAJ) has officially removed Sheikh Umar Ibrahim Imam from his position as National Imam. In a press release dated November 4, the Council announced the passing of a Vote of No Confidence against the religious leader, citing constitutional violations and misconduct. According to the statement, the decision was made pursuant to Article (11)(3) of the ASWAJ Constitution, which empowers the Council to remove the National Imam following a vote of no confidence supported by the required majority. The Council stated that it had previously issued a notice to Sheikh Umar Ibrahim Imam on October 18, 2026, detailing allegations against him and providing a deadline of October 27, 2026, to respond. However, the Council notes that as of the date of the resolution, no formal written or verbal response was received from the Office of the Imam. The Vote The resolution was passed during a meeting of the National Da’awa Council, the body mandated to elect and remove the National Imam and his deputies. Out of the members present, Twenty-one (21) voted in favor of the removal. Four members were recorded as absent: Sheikh Dr. Bashir Adam, Sheikh Zackaria Addo, Sheikh Khidir Adam, and Sheikh Dr. Abbass Sakhr. Consequential Orders Following the adoption of the resolution, the Council has declared the office of the National Imam vacant. Several consequential orders have been issued to ensure a smooth transition: Handover: Sheikh Umar Ibrahim Imam is required to hand over all ASWAJ properties, official documents, stamps, records, and other institutional assets to the appropriate authorized officer immediately. Notification: Relevant registration authorities, financial institutions, and stakeholders are to be formally notified of the change in leadership. Succession: Arrangements are to be made for the election of a substantive National Imam in accordance with the ASWAJ Constitution. Call for Calm Concluding the press release, the National Da’awa Council called on all members and stakeholders of ASWAJ to remain calm and uphold the Constitution. “The Council calls on all members and stakeholders… to preserve peace, unity, and the integrity of the organization,” the statement read. The development marks a significant shift in the leadership of the organization, effective immediately as of November 4, 2026.

items.title: Makkah Defence Alliance secretary general to assume duties in Riyadh soon: FO
items.description: The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday said that the secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance, retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood, is expected to assume his responsibilities in Riyadh soon. Mahmood was appointed on Sep 23 as the first secretary general of the alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed on Aug 7, empowers the three members to consider an armed attack on one member an attack on all. Speaking at the FO’s weekly press briefing on Friday, Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan further said that the three members would jointly decide on convening a meeting of their alliance. The Makkah Defence Alliance has garnered particular attention as Saudi Arabia faces attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, including a deadly strike that closed Riyadh’s international airport for two weeks last month. Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks, the military’s spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said in mid-October. However, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) director general also clarified that all members of the Makkah Defence Alliance were “absolutely clear […] that this alliance has no offensive intent; it is purely defensive”. The DG ISPR added: “Pakistan is giving very strong signals that this collective deterrence is at play, has already been actualised and we will take all necessary steps for the security and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Haramain Sharifain (The Two Holy Mosques).” Islamabad has two defence pacts with Riyadh aimed at collective deterrence — the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement that also includes Turkiye. On Thursday, the Turkish parliament approved a bill ratifying the Makkah pact , paving the way for the trilateral security pact to come into force. On its part, FO said late last month that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already completed the ratification processes, noting that each country followed its own constitutional and legal procedures to approve and ratify international agreements. Pakistan, others actively making efforts for peace in Middle East In his briefing, Khan also touched upon the crisis in the Gulf, saying that Pakistan would continue its efforts to facilitate dialogue in the conflict involving Iran and the United States. He said Islamabad had brought the two parties under one roof despite them having remained out of contact for decades and supported a peaceful resolution through dialogue and diplomacy. Khan cited the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the warring parties on June 18 as “a testament to Pakistan’s commitment to […] promoting peace and stability in our region”. He added that Pakistan, Qatar and other countries were actively contributing to mediation efforts. The FO official emphasised that peace in the region must be established through “political dialogue and diplomacy” rather than war. While acknowledging that the process of negotiations could be time-consuming, Khan asserted, “I believe that peace will eventually prevail and that countries will be able to resolve these matters peacefully.” Elaborating further, the FO spokesperson said Israel was playing the role of a “spoiler” in the ongoing US-Iran war. Criticising Israel’s expansionist policies, he said peace in the region was not in Israel’s interest and that its expansionist ambitions were among the major causes of the current regional crisis. These ambitions were not limited to Iran, he said, adding that Palestine, Syria, Lebanon and other countries in the region were also affected by Israel’s expansionist designs. When asked about the recent midterm elections in the US, the FO spokesperson said elections were an internal matter of that country and reiterated that Pakistan maintained close relations with Washington. Democrats seized control of the US Congress earlier this week, capturing the Senate and House of Representatives in a stunning, nationwide rejection of Donald Trump set to put the brakes on the final two years of his presidency. None harmed in strike on LNG tanker The FO spokesperson was also asked about a vessel carrying Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) to Karachi, Al Mayeda, being hit by projectiles last week. Shah said none of the 25 crew on board, including Pakistani nationals, were injured when the LNG carrier was hit while “transiting eastbound through the Persian Gulf in international waters”. “The incident caused a small fire on board, but all crew members remained unharmed,” he said, adding that the vessel returned to Qatar. “The concerned Pakistani authorities are coordinating with the relevant parties to establish further details of the incident,” he added. The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) strongly condemned the attack on the tanker on Sunday, describing it as a “dangerous escalation”. Doha also denounced the targeting of the tanker “a dangerous act that threatens the safety of maritime navigation and the security of global energy supplies”.

Sunday Bamidele Aro as the authentic winner of the Kogi West primary election. The court ruling put to rest the legal tussle that followed Senator Karimi’s move to transfer the case from the Federal High Court in Lokoja to the Abuja division. The chieftain also distanced himself from ongoing political talks with the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Kogi West, shooting down the narrative that the APC cannot win the district without Karimi. He called on Senator Karimi to work for the candidate declared by the court of law and throw his weight behind all APC candidates, from the presidency down to the state assembly. Furthermore, Ibrahim urged Karimi’s supporters to change gear, describing Sam Aro as a credible person who has been tested, trusted, and found worthy. While congratulating the candidate, Ibrahim asked Aro to hit the ground running, assuring him that supporters are ready to work alongside him. items.title: Newsroom bomb threats follow escalating European flight hoaxes
items.description: Newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria received emailed bomb threats on Friday from a purported “Mikhail Andropov”, claiming responsibility for a widening wave of hoax threats disrupting passenger flights across Europe. The messages, sent to Bulgaria’s Nova TV and the Irish public broadcaster RTE , which evacuated its offices and suspended programming, were headlined “Message to the West” and portrayed the threats as the prelude to a series of attacks on means of transport across Europe. The British broadcaster Sky also said it had received a security threat. Reuters was not able to establish the identity of the sender, the origin of the emails, or whether they had in fact come from the same source as the threats to any or all of the dozens of flights affected since Tuesday. But they added to concern among European officials that the hoaxes are part of a campaign of “hybrid” disruptions, which many have blamed on Russia, aimed at countries that have helped Ukraine. Moscow has denied involvement. Spanish Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares said Europe appeared to be facing “hybrid aggression and a form of psychological warfare”. No explosive devices were found and all planes, including those threatened on Friday, landed safely. Flight disruptions lessen Security experts said on Thursday that the threats might be intended to punish European nations that have armed or financed Ukraine as it resists the full-scale invasion Russia launched in 2022. It was also possible, however, that individuals were laying false trails, issuing copycat threats or acting on personal grievances. Around half a dozen flights were disrupted in some way on Tuesday and more than two dozen on Thursday, some of them making unplanned landings or being escorted to their destinations by fighter jets. On Friday, an Italian airport authority source said a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome had been diverted to Venice but, despite more than a dozen hoax threats, overall there was far less direct disruption to air travel. Hungarian jets did, however, escort airliners flying from Brussels to Sofia and from Prague to Bucharest and Cyprus through Hungarian airspace. Danish police said on Friday they were investigating threats directed at air traffic at Copenhagen airport, but that their immediate assessment was that there had been no danger to passengers. The airport said it was “operating normally”. Czech police said they had registered bomb threats to flights departing from and arriving in Prague. An airport spokesperson said they concerned four inbound and five outbound flights, but that no explosive devices had been found and no flights had been cancelled or diverted as a result. The French prime minister’s office said four new bomb threats had been made to aircraft flying over French territory, and that all had landed safely. A bomb alert on a Ryanair flight from Rome to Lisbon prompted a security operation when it landed, CNN Portugal reported. A fire truck is parked in front of the Vaclav Havel Airport in Prague as bomb threats forced airliners to make unplanned landings across Europe, in Prague, Czech Republic, on November 5, 2026. — Reuters Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said Nato had ordered some air patrols in the area, the first report that the Western defence alliance had become involved. While no country attributed blame for the threats, they follow a wave of sabotage attacks and attempts on targets across Europe ranging from German electricity substations to defence-related facilities in the Baltic region, and supermarket refrigerators in France and elsewhere. Germany blamed Russia directly for a drone attack on Leipzig airport. EU commissioner says Russia is often to blame for attacks Security experts said on Thursday that the threats had the hallmarks of a coordinated “hybrid attack”, although it was always possible that individuals were issuing copycat threats or acting on personal grievances. Many officials have linked the campaign to Europe’s support for Ukraine in its war against Russian invasion , accusing Moscow of a campaign of “hybrid” disruptions that are essentially cheap to execute, easily deniable, and not expected to trigger an armed response. Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares told the national broadcaster TVE that, while it would take time to determine exactly what happened, “it cannot be mere coincidence that so many incidents with exactly the same modus operandi are happening across Europe”. “The most reasonable assumption is that we are facing an attempt at hybrid aggression and a form of psychological warfare,” he said, adding that Europe must be prepared for more such challenges. European technology commissioner Henna Virkkunen told Reuters on Thursday that since 2022 Europe had faced a range of hybrid operations including sabotage of critical infrastructure, drone incursions, cyber breaches and election interference. “We are under attack all the time,” she said. “The reason behind these operations is to destabilise our societies and create mistrust among our citizens.” It’s not always Russia who is behind different hybrid operations,” she said, adding: “Quite often it is Russia.” On Thursday, an airport source in Italy said bomb threats had been sent to several airlines and airport operators in Rome and Milan purporting to be from “fighters of the Male State”, a far-right anti-feminist movement banned in Russia. Reuters could not confirm who had sent the email. Vladislav Pozdnyakov, a Russian blogger who set up Male State in 2016, said it no longer existed and was not involved in any way.

items.title: Zineb Redouani s'engage avec l'espagnol FC Badalona
items.description: Le club espagnol FC Badalona Women a annoncé vendredi la signature de l'internationale marocaine Zineb Redouani, en provenance de l'AS FAR, pour renforcer sa défense en Liga F Moeve. Âgée de 26 ans, la latérale marocaine a déclaré, dans un communiqué du club catalan, être « très heureuse » de rejoindre cette formation et d'évoluer dans « un championnat aussi compétitif que la Liga espagnole, réputée pour sa grande exigence technique et tactique ». Formée au Raja Aïn Harrouda, Zineb Redouani a rejoint l'AS FAR en 2020, avec lequel elle a remporté sept titres de championne du Maroc et six Coupes du Trône, et disputé deux finales de la Ligue des champions africaine. Avec la sélection nationale, la Lionne de l'Atlas a atteint la finale de la Coupe d'Afrique des Nations (CAN) féminine 2022. Ses performances lors de cette compétition lui ont valu une place dans l'équipe-type du tournoi, ainsi que dans le onze idéal de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) la même année. Ce recrutement intervient alors que le FC Badalona Women est pénalisé par plusieurs absences défensives, notamment celle de Berta Pujadas, opérée d'une lésion du ménisque du genou droit et éloignée des terrains pour plusieurs mois. Rapide et à l'aise dans le jeu de combinaison, Redouani devrait apporter du dynamisme sur les côtés de la défense catalane. La nouvelle recrue marocaine, qui a déjà pris part à trois séances d'entraînement avec son nouveau club, pourrait faire ses débuts lundi face à l'Atlético de Madrid. items.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
items.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday. So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases have been reported across the country of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency. That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991. State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children. Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease. Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death. Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year in the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide. items.title: Tanzanian Court Convicts Opposition Leader of Incitement
items.description: Click to expand Image Tanzanian opposition leader and CHADEMA chairman Tundu Lissu waves to supporters at the High Court in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, November 6, 2026. © 2026 AP Photo/Florence Majani Tanzania’s High Court on November 6 convicted Tundu Lissu, the leader of Tanzania’s main opposition party, Chama Cha Demokrasia Na Maendeleo (the ‘Party of Democracy and Development’, or CHADEMA), of incitement, sentencing him to four years in prison. The judges acquitted him of treason, a charge that carries the death penalty. Authorities accused him of having planned to instigate the public to obstruct the October 2025 elections, based on remarks he made at an April 3, 2025, rally in Dar es Salaam. CHADEMA had been calling for the government to undertake “fundamental electoral reforms” as part of its campaign, “No Reforms, No Elections.” Prior to his conviction, Lissu had been imprisoned without bail since his April 9, 2025 arrest. The proceedings against Lissu raised serious human rights concerns. His trial faced repeated delays, and he represented himself after saying the authorities had denied him private access to his lawyers. In May 2025, Tanzanian authorities abducted, beat, tortured, and deported activists who had traveled from neighboring Kenya and Uganda to Dar es Salaam to observe the proceedings. President Samia Suluhu Hassan subsequently instructed the Tanzanian security agencies to take action against foreign people who she claimed were “invading and interfering in our affairs.” Lissu’s conviction is the latest example of Tanzania’s repression of political opponents. For years, the authorities have arbitrarily arrested and charged opposition figures for allegedly inciting protests and terrorism. They escalated these arrests following widespread violence around the October 2025 elections, which the government has accused the opposition, including Lissu, of organizing. In May 2026, unknown people abducted and beat Lissu’s personal assistant, David Djumbe, in Dar es Salaam, before he escaped. The police denied involvement and announced an investigation but have not reported any arrests. CHADEMA said 51 of its officials were arrested and charged with terrorism after the government banned all political rallies ahead of youth-led protests planned for July 7. The authorities arrested and charged John Pambalu, a CHADEMA official, with treason in October, and Coletha Clavery Ntidyicha, the chair of a regional youth wing, with “counselling the commission of terrorist acts” on November 3. The Tanzanian government should end its crackdown on political opponents and their supporters and stop weaponizing the criminal justice system to silence dissent.

items.title: Mbappe headlines Zidane’s France squad, Pagis gets call-up
items.description: Kylian Mbappe headlined the France squad named Friday by coach Zinedine Zidane for their Nations League matches against Italy and Turkey after picking up an injury on international duty in September, while Pablo Pagis was handed a debut call-up. Real Madrid superstar Mbappe, the France captain, scored the winner in Zidane’s first match in charge of Les Bleus away to Turkey on September 25, but suffered a knee injury in the same game that ruled him out of the team’s three remaining fixtures of the last international window. Without him, France won twice against Belgium, in Brussels and then at home, and drew in between against Italy. Mbappe has since returned to action for his club, scoring eight times in seven matches between La Liga and the Champions League. France are without Paris Saint-Germain star Ousmane Dembele and Rennes striker Esteban Lepaul for this month’s double-header, so Marcus Thuram of Inter Milan is recalled to an attack which will also feature Pagis for the first time. The 23-year-old Pagis, who plays chiefly as an attacking midfielder, is rewarded for his impressive form this season since joining Paris FC — who are fourth in Ligue 1 — from Lorient. Pagis is the son of Mickael Pagis, the former Marseille player who at one time appeared for the France beach soccer team coached by Eric Cantona. Aurelien Tchouameni of Real Madrid returns in midfield in place of Manu Kone after missing the last international window, while Manchester United’s Leny Yoro and Chelsea’s Malo Gusto replace Jules Kounde of Barcelona and Maxence Lacroix of Chelsea in the defence. Zidane’s side play Italy in Milan next Thursday, November 12, and then take on Turkey in Bordeaux three days later in their final group-stage fixtures. They are top of Nations League Group A1 with 10 points from four outings, three ahead of Italy. The top two teams in the group will advance to the quarter-finals next March. items.title: AES : intégration régionale et développement économique au cœur des échanges entre les dirigeants
items.description: Le president de la Transition, le general d'armee Assimi Goïta, a effectue le 5 novembre 2026 une visite de travail au Burkina Faso et au Niger. Ce deplacement avait pour objectif de consolider les relations entre les trois pays membres de la Confederation des etats du Sahel AES et de renforcer leur cooperation dans plusieurs domaines. a Ouagadougou comme a Niamey, les discussions ont porte principalement sur la securite, l'integration regionale et le developpement economique. Au Burkina Faso, le general d'armee Assimi Goïta s'est entretenu avec le capitaine Ibrahim Traore, president de la Transition burkinabe. Les deux dirigeants ont notamment evoque le renforcement de la cooperation militaire et des actions securitaires au sein de l'AES. Les echanges ont egalement porte sur les projets de developpement economique et les perspectives d'integration regionale entre les pays de la Confederation. Un engagement commun contre le terrorisme a Niamey, le president malien a rencontre son homologue nigerien, le general Abdourahamane Tiani. Les discussions ont notamment ete consacrees a la lutte contre le terrorisme. Les deux chefs d'etat ont salue les actions menees par la Force unifiee de l'AES et reaffirme leur engagement commun dans la lutte contre l'insecurite dans l'espace confederal. Au-dela des questions securitaires, plusieurs secteurs economiques ont egalement ete abordes. Il s'agit notamment de la libre circulation des personnes et des biens, des transports, de l'agro-industrie ainsi que de la valorisation des ressources minieres et energetiques. Cette tournee s'inscrit dans la volonte des trois pays de renforcer leur cooperation et de consolider les mecanismes de leur integration au sein de l' AES . items.title: Osimhen sustains knee injury, to miss Nigeria’s AFCON qualifiers
items.description: Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen is set to undergo knee surgery after sustaining an injury during Galatasaray’s UEFA Champions League clash against VfB Stuttgart. The Turkish champions confirmed on Friday that the Nigerian forward suffered a strain in his left knee, with an MRI scan revealing a loose body in the affected area. In a statement, Galatasaray said Osimhen would undergo arthroscopic knee surgery on Saturday at Maslak Acıbadem Hospital under the supervision of the club’s doctor, Yener İnce. The statement read: “Our player Victor Osimhen, who suffered a strain in his left knee during our UEFA Champions League match against VfB Stuttgart and was found to have a loose body in MRI scans, is scheduled to undergo arthroscopic knee surgery tomorrow at Maslak Acıbadem Hospital, performed by our club doctor Yener İnce.” The club also confirmed that the 26-year-old had been withdrawn from the squad for its next fixture against Amed S. F. Osimhen’s injury is a major setback for Nigeria, with the striker now expected to miss the Super Eagles’ Africa Cup of Nations qualifying fixtures against Tanzania on November 13 and 17. His absence would leave Nigeria without one of its most influential attacking players as the national team prepares for the upcoming international fixtures. The Super Eagles will hope for a successful operation and a quick recovery for the Galatasaray forward, although the club is yet to announce an expected return date.\ Vanguard News The post Osimhen sustains knee injury, to miss Nigeria’s AFCON qualifiers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Customs begins evacuation of 98 abandoned power equipment containers
items.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has commenced the evacuation of 98 containers of electricity transmission equipment abandoned at Nigerian ports for between 14 and 20 years. The first batch of 44 containers was released on Friday at ENL Consortium Terminal, Apapa Port, Lagos, by the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, and the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe. The exercise followed a presidential directive to recover the stranded equipment and accelerate the rehabilitation of the country’s electricity transmission network. The consignments, imported for government-backed projects through the Federal Ministry of Power, Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) and Niger Delta Power Holding Company, include transformers, electrical cables, switchgears and other transmission materials. Speaking at the event, Adeniyi said the release followed President Bola Tinubu’s directive after the Minister of Power presented the matter to the Federal Executive Council. He said Customs had introduced priority processing, dedicated examination officers and approved waivers on relevant charges to facilitate the evacuation. Adeniyi, however, described the abandonment of government-funded equipment by contractors as economic sabotage, warning that those responsible would be identified and could face sanctions, including blacklisting. He said the recovered equipment would undergo technical assessment, with serviceable materials deployed to ongoing and stalled transmission projects, while obsolete ones would be disposed of in line with regulations. In his remarks, Tegbe said the abandonment had stalled transmission projects for nearly two decades, limiting network expansion and placing additional pressure on existing substations. He listed Kaduna, Osun, Nasarawa and Cross River among states expected to benefit from the recovered equipment, which he said would improve transmission capacity, strengthen electricity evacuation and reduce supply interruptions. The minister assured that the equipment would not be abandoned again, adding that technical teams had commenced identifying projects for their deployment. He said the government was targeting the evacuation of the remaining containers within one month. Meanwhile, shipping companies and terminal operators pledged their cooperation to ensure the consignments were evacuated without further delay.
