items.title: Institute of Packaging Ghana to strengthen collaboration with farmers, agribusinesses to boost packaging industry
items.description: The Institute of Packaging, Ghana (IOPG) says it will deepen collaboration with farmers, agro-processors and other stakeholders in the agricultural value chain to improve packaging solutions, reduce post-harvest losses and enhance the competitiveness of locally produced goods. The initiative forms part of the Institute’s commitment to positioning packaging as a strategic tool for agricultural transformation and industrial development as it marks its 23rd anniversary. This was captured in a statement issued by the Institute on November 3. As part of the anniversary celebrations, IOPG will organise a Packaging Webinar on December 2, 2026, ahead of Ghana’s National Farmers’ Day celebrations. The webinar, themed “Packaging as a Strategic Asset: Building Brand Loyalty and Driving Agricultural Value Creation,” will bring together farmers, agro-processors, packaging manufacturers, researchers, policymakers and other private-sector players to explore opportunities for collaboration. According to the Institute, “the engagement will provide a platform for knowledge sharing and stakeholder discussions on agricultural value addition, post-harvest loss reduction, brand development, market access, export competitiveness and sustainable packaging innovation.” IOPG noted that packaging must go beyond simply containing and protecting products to become an important business tool for adding value, building strong brands and increasing profitability. The Institute has also called on government agencies, industry associations, educational institutions and private-sector organisations to invest in appropriate and innovative packaging solutions to unlock the potential of Ghana’s agricultural resources. IOPG 23RD ANNIVERSARY PRESS RELEASE FIN- Nov 3, 2026 Download Since its inauguration in 2003, IOPG has provided professional training, research, advocacy, consultancy and business advisory services to industry players and small and medium-sized enterprises. It says these interventions are aimed at reducing post-harvest losses, enhancing food security, improving industrial productivity and expanding domestic and international trade. The December webinar is being organised in collaboration with Royal Crown Packaging Limited, the Chamber of Agribusiness Ghana, Qualiplast Ghana Limited and ePack Flexible Packaging.

items.title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument
items.description: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order that he says will prevent future presidents from making certain changes to the White House Oval Office. The executive order declares the president’s official office, which he has renovated, to be a national monument. “We’re making it a national monument, and it will not be allowed to be touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people, in order to build something in a slightly different shape,” Trump told reporters on Thursday. The order does not prevent future presidents from changing the decor of the famous room. The document says that it does not “restrict the President’s authority to redecorate the monument, select furnishings, or make ordinary operational and security modifications that do not substantially impair the monument’s historic structure or architectural character”. American presidents currently have the power to make some changes to the White House but large projects require the permission of Congress. The order comes months after Trump tore down the entirety of the White House East Wing in a project that has faced legal challenges. The project was not approved by the US Congress. Construction has continued, with plans to turn the space into a new ballroom. Signing the new executive order on Thursday, the president said: “We like the Oval Office, and it’s a symbol, like the White House itself. It’s a symbol of our country and the greatness of our country.” He added that world leaders who have visited in recent months have complimented his decorative changes to the room. Trump said the White House and the Oval Office had been in need of repairs before his changes, calling it “badly damaged”. He described broken windows, cracked walls and broken stone. Many of the noticeable changes, though, were cosmetic, including a large gold plaque reading “Oval Office” outside the space, paving over the Rose Garden and adding a new helicopter pad. Trump said the order would “make it impossible for anybody ever to destroy this incredible space”. It is unclear whether this action could simply be reversed by a future president or a legal challenge. Most executive orders can be overturned and Trump himself scaled back two national monuments in Utah in 2017. But revoking a national monument designation has not yet been tested in court. The White House grounds are already designated as a National Historic Landmark, which is intended to prevent against sudden changes to the building. Trump’s order calls on the Oval Office to be maintained by the National Park Service “in a manner that protects its historic character, architectural integrity, and association with the Presidency”. It notes the existing protections to the White House, but says “nonetheless, the Oval Office merits specific recognition and protective management as a discrete historic structure of national significance”. Congress has carved out an exemption to the National Historic Preservation Act, in order to allow presidents to make needed changes. The current Oval Office has existed since the early 1930s, after its conception by President Franklin D Roosevelt. Greg Werkheiser, from the law firm Cultural Heritage Partners, which specialises in historic preservation, says that temporary alterations like “furniture and decor is completely up to the president’s discretion”. “As long as they’re not damaging the permanent art and architecture, they can generally do whatever they want,” he told the BBC. Werkheiser argues that the Trump administration has shown disregard for other historic sites in Washington and, through lawsuits, has attempted to undermine the laws that require preservation. He called Trump’s order “hypocrisy”, noting the various projects he’s pushed for across Washington – including plans to build a new triumphal arch, which has been temporarily put on hold by a federal judge. “On the one hand he’s talking about the importance of preserving the Oval Office – which is legally meaningless because he can’t do it – and on the other hand he is absolutely taking an axe to the law that allows us to preserve other historic sites.”

items.title: Plateforme « Cercle V » : « Ville Verte », un espace de dialogue entre art, architecture et territoire
items.description: Avec le concours du Fonds Ndary Lo, la nouvelle plateforme culturelle a été lancée jeudi au Goethe-Institut de Dakar. Son premier chapitre mêle sculptures, danse et débat sur l’habiter collectif. L’équation du « vivre ensemble quand les villes se transforment », est au cœur de la plateforme culturelle de Ville Verte « Cercle V », lancée jeudi au Goethe-Institut de Dakar. Intitulé « Une place parmi les autres », le premier chapitre, placé sous la direction artistique de la curatrice Aïsha Dème, fait dialoguer les sculptures de Ndary Lo et une performance de la chorégraphe Khoudia Touré. Il s’achève sur une conversation entre un artiste, un bâtisseur de la terre crue et une sociologue. A lire aussi : Culture : Le musée des Civilisations noires, un portrait de la négritude Avec Cercle V, « Ville Verte », affirme une conviction : celle d’une ville qui se construit aussi par la culture et le dialogue. Conçue comme un espace de réflexion indépendant, la plateforme laisse la parole aux artistes, aux chercheurs et aux praticiens. Ce premier chapitre en appelle d’autres. « Construire des lieux ne suffit pas. Ce qui fait véritablement exister un lieu, ce sont les histoires qu’il accueille, les rencontres qu’il rend possibles et les conversations qu’il provoque », a déclaré Abdoul Wahab Kane, directeur général de Ville Verte, qui a ouvert la soirée. Ndary Lo, le fer à béton fait silhouette Le Fonds Ndary Lo a prêté plusieurs sculptures de l’artiste, disparu en 2017. Ndary Lo avait fait du fer à béton, matériau qui arme les constructions sans qu’on le voie, la matière de silhouettes humaines devenues emblématiques de l’art contemporain sénégalais. Formé à l’École nationale des Beaux-Arts de Dakar, deux fois lauréat du Grand Prix Léopold Sédar Senghor de la Biennale de Dakar (2002 et 2008), il a vu son œuvre rayonner bien au-delà du Sénégal. Réunies au Goethe-Institut, ses figures, présences distinctes qui partagent un même espace, donnent le ton de la soirée : ce que l’on garde pour soi, ce que l’on met en commun, et la place que chacun y trouve. Les œuvres ont d’abord résonné avec la performance de Khoudia Touré. Fondatrice de la Compagnie Khor, la chorégraphe franco-sénégalaise développe une écriture hybride qui mêle hip-hop, house, krump et danses traditionnelles sénégalaises. M. DIEME

items.title: Over 400 Northern Ashanti Mines workers petition Mahama over mine closure
items.description: More than 400 workers of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited Company (NAMLC) have petitioned President John Mahama to intervene in the closure of the mine and facilitate its reopening following its takeover by the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS). The workers presented their petition to the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) for Asante Akim Central, Rev. Dr Ebenezer Ekow Aidoo, on November 6, appealing to the President to consider the impact of the closure on their livelihoods and the wider local economy. Presenting the petition on behalf of the workers, the company’s Community Relations Officer, Amponsah Alfred Oduro, said employees were left stranded after the mine was taken over on Friday, October 22, and they were given just three hours to vacate the premises. According to him, the short notice meant several workers could not retrieve their personal belongings before leaving the site. Some employees who were away on break also had their belongings locked up in company bungalows and offices, where they remain. The workers said the closure had left more than 430 employees without their main source of income, pushing hundreds of households and thousands of dependants into financial difficulty. They further explained that more than 40 per cent of the company’s workforce came from host communities, meaning the closure had affected not only direct employees but also local businesses, suppliers, transport operators and other service providers who depended on the mine. While acknowledging the government’s responsibility to protect the country’s natural resources and enforce mining laws, the workers appealed for a compassionate and constructive approach to resolving the issues that led to the termination of the company’s mining lease. The employees said the closure came at a time when Northern Ashanti Mines was undertaking major expansion projects expected to create significant employment opportunities. They disclosed that the company was constructing a processing plant scheduled for commissioning in the first quarter of 2027. It had also begun stockpiling mined ore in preparation for the next phase of operations. In addition, the workers said the company had procured 17 forty-foot containers of equipment, which were currently stranded at the port awaiting customs clearance. According to them, completing the processing plant was expected to generate more than 1,000 direct and indirect jobs, providing further employment opportunities for people in the surrounding communities. The closure has also disrupted the company’s training and employment programmes for young Ghanaians. The workers disclosed that more than 40 Ghanaian graduates were enrolled in the company’s Graduate Traineeship Programme, while another 50 were undergoing onboarding. They also said more than 50 National Service positions had been earmarked for the 2026/2027 service year, but the planned opportunities had been affected by the shutdown. The employees said the mine represented more than a place of work, as their jobs provided for their families and offered them a means of securing their future. They therefore appealed to President Mahama, the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, the Minerals Commission, traditional authorities, organised labour and civil society organisations to explore all lawful options for reopening the mine. They stressed that their appeal was not intended to undermine the government’s responsibility to enforce mining regulations but to secure an opportunity to return to work and earn a living. The workers called for constructive engagement among the relevant stakeholders to address the concerns surrounding the mine’s closure while considering the economic consequences for employees and host communities. Receiving the petition on behalf of President Mahama, Rev. Dr Ebenezer Ekow Aidoo assured the workers that their concerns would be forwarded to the appropriate authorities for consideration. He commended them for choosing a lawful and peaceful approach to seeking redress rather than resorting to actions that could worsen the situation.

items.title: Festival de la grenade : la 20ᵉ édition s’ouvre à Khalfia
items.description: Lancée jeudi dans la commune de Khalfia, la manifestation se poursuit jusqu’au dimanche 8 novembre. Plus de 23 troupes de tbourida ont pris part à la cérémonie d’ouverture, qui coïncide avec le 51ᵉ anniversaire de la Marche Verte. Le centre de la commune de Khalfia, dans la province de Fquih Ben Salah, a accueilli, jeudi 5 novembre 2026, la cérémonie d’ouverture de la 20ᵉ édition du Festival national de la grenade, qui se poursuit jusqu’au dimanche 8 novembre. Organisée sous le thème « Vingt éditions de fidélité à la grenade… et un parcours au service de la valorisation du patrimoine et du développement », cette cérémonie a été présidée par Mohamed Karnachi, gouverneur de la province. Une délégation officielle, des élus, des acteurs locaux et des représentants de la société civile y ont pris part. La cérémonie a été ponctuée de spectacles folkloriques mettant à l’honneur les traditions locales, régionales et nationales, ainsi que de prestations de tbourida. Plus de 23 troupes de tbourida, ou sorbas, venues de différentes localités de la région, ont participé à ces démonstrations. Celles-ci figurent parmi les temps forts du festival et témoignent de l’attachement de la région à son patrimoine équestre. À cette occasion, Abdelilah Salam, président du conseil communal de Khalfia, a mis en avant l’histoire et les sites patrimoniaux de la région, notamment la Kasbah Zaidania, ainsi que la qualité et les caractéristiques propres à la grenade d’Ouled Abdellah. Il a souligné que le festival contribue à faire connaître et à valoriser ce produit, conformément aux Hautes Orientations Royales en faveur des produits du terroir et du développement des zones rurales. Le responsable communal a également relevé que le programme réunit des activités culturelles, scientifiques, récréatives et sportives. L’exposition des produits du terroir, à laquelle participent des coopératives et des producteurs locaux, constitue, a-t-il indiqué, une occasion de faire découvrir leurs produits et de soutenir leur commercialisation. Pour sa part, Mustapha Raouf, président de l’Association du Festival de la grenade pour le développement rural intégré – Ouled Abdellah, a expliqué que cette 20ᵉ édition permet de renouveler la rencontre entre les habitants et les visiteurs, tout en faisant connaître les atouts et le patrimoine d’Ouled Abdellah. Il a ajouté que l’association entend inscrire le festival dans la durée, comme un rendez-vous annuel consacré à la grenade et offrant aux coopératives et aux producteurs un espace de rencontre avec le public. Au programme figurent des prestations de tbourida, une exposition de produits agricoles et du terroir, des animations artistiques ainsi que des rencontres consacrées à l’investissement et au patrimoine de Zaidania. Le festival associe ainsi la promotion de la grenade, l’un des principaux produits de la région, à la mise en valeur de la fantasia traditionnelle et du patrimoine culturel et historique local. Cette édition coïncide avec le 51ᵉ anniversaire de la Marche Verte et intervient après la célébration de la Fête de l’Unité. Elle met également en lumière l’histoire de la région et son patrimoine, notamment la Kasbah Zaidania, contribuant ainsi à faire connaître ses atouts culturels et touristiques. Cette manifestation s’inscrit dans les efforts visant à valoriser les atouts locaux, à soutenir les produits du terroir et à préserver le patrimoine, en cohérence avec les Hautes Orientations Royales en faveur du développement du monde rural. La 20ᵉ édition entend ainsi renforcer la notoriété de la grenade d’Ouled Abdellah, élargir les possibilités de la faire connaître et de la commercialiser, et soutenir la dynamique économique et culturelle de la région. Le festival est organisé par l’Association du Festival de la grenade pour le développement rural intégré – Ouled Abdellah, en partenariat avec la commune de Khalfia, avec le soutien du Conseil de la région de Béni Mellal-Khénifra, de la Société Atlas de Développement Touristique de la Région Béni Mellal-Khénifra et de l’Association Oum Er-Rbia pour le développement intégré – Fquih Ben Salah. Participent également à son organisation le Groupe OCP, l’Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique, l’Office National du Conseil Agricole, l’Office Régional de Mise en Valeur Agricole du Tadla et la Direction régionale de la Culture de Béni Mellal-Khénifra. items.title: Spate of bomb threats poses serious challenge to airline industry
items.description: With no fewer than 32 bomb threats affecting a dozen airlines in the space of four days, the aviation industry is facing another potential crisis. Some of the threats apparently came from phone calls, others via email, and although they have all turned out to be hoaxes, they were each clearly serious enough to force emergency action. Some planes had to be escorted by military jets, others were quietly inspected mid-air by cabin crew – desperate not to cause alarm. A number had to be re-routed from their original destinations, landing at different airports, sometimes in different countries. An Aer Lingus flight had to land at an airbase 1,000 kilometers from its intended destination after running low on fuel. All this poses a serious challenge to the airlines, who have little idea who is causing the severe disruption they have faced almost every day this week. Although so far all threats have turned out to be hoaxes, airlines have no choice but take each threat seriously. “They have a triage system, but follow the same protocols for each until they are absolutely sure there is no threat,” says Marco Chan, a former commercial airline pilot and aviation expert at Kingston University. “That could involve a mid-air inspection, but definitely a search once the plane has landed. “Passengers might not even know there is an issue until they are told to disembark. It can cause disruption, but that is a small price to pay when safety is at stake”, he adds. The sight of sniffer dogs and specialist teams on the tarmac searching for explosives on commercial planes may cause alarm. So far, the disruption too has been limited to the few thousand passengers who have been directly involved. Paul Mason, an aviation security expert, says there will be a financial cost to the airline involved, but planes get diverted every day. “The number can sometimes run to over a hundred planes daily, for things like technical issues, medical emergencies, even the weather,” he adds. “They far outweigh the few which have been diverted due to hoaxes. So airlines are well equipped at dealing with the unexpected.” It is also unlikely that customers will be able to get refunds, he explains, because these incidents are not the fault of the airlines. The more worrying aspect over the past few days will be the seeming random nature of the targets and the lack of any credible intelligence regarding who is behind the threats. Aside from emails suggesting that an extremist misogynist group had claimed responsibility for a handful of the incidents – although since denied by its founder – there appear to be few leads. With 20 years of military experience as well, Paul Mason says the incidents bear the hallmarks of hybrid warfare, which involves unconventional methods such as cyber attacks. “It does feel co-ordinated,” he says. “Russia has said it’s got nothing to do with it, but it could be proxies. It’s a very easy way to create disruption and chaos, with plausible deniability.” “That’s the problem. Someone can have an opinion on who is behind it, but if the perpetrators are using sophisticated technology, it will be very hard to trace them.” He does say however that if misguided individuals try to copy the threats they could find themselves in serious trouble. The Aviation Security Act 1982 states that “intentionally communicating false, misleading, or deceptive information that endangers – or is likely to endanger – the safety of an aircraft in flight is a serious criminal offense”. The maximum sentence is life imprisonment. There is precious little that airports and airlines can do to guard against actually receiving threats, as they can come from a vast range of sources. But the punishment is designed to act as a deterrent. As Paul Mason warns: “Someone might think it’s a laugh and very easy to do, but unless they are very sophisticated, they are highly likely to be traced. And find themselves facing prison.”

items.title: Prioritise youth employment – TEIN, TESCON to NDC, NPP
items.description: The Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN) of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) and the Tertiary Students’ Confederacy Network (TESCON) of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) have appealed to their respective political parties to make youth employment a priority and to complete all projects started by earlier governments when in power. The appeal was contained in a joint communiqué issued in Tamale last Saturday following a workshop on Political Inclusion and Consensus Building: The Role of Political Parties and Parliament. It was organised by the African Centre for Parliamentary Affairs (ACEPA) with support from the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA). They pledged to sustain the dialogue beyond the workshop and to explore joint activities that build trust, tolerance and cooperation among young political leaders. Employment The TEIN and TESCON encouraged their parties to adopt sustainable policies that expand economic opportunities, promote entrepreneurship, strengthen skills development and address unemployment and underemployment among young people. They also proposed a national development plan that goes beyond party lines and sets shared long-term priorities to support policy consistency, continuity and sustainable progress. The two tertiary student networks noted that they came from different political traditions and perspectives, but said their differences “do not make us enemies”. They described themselves as citizens of one nation under one Constitution, pointing to the civic responsibilities set out in Article 41 of the 1992 Constitution. In the communiqué, they pledged to treat political opponents as fellow citizens and valued participants in democracy, and to keep debates focused on ideas and policies, steering clear of insults, character assassination, stereotyping, intimidation and political violence. They also promised to communicate responsibly on television, radio and social media by verifying information and rejecting misinformation and disinformation. On campus, they committed to peaceful, lawful and credible elections, discouraging intimidation, electoral misconduct and the use of unofficial security groups, while protecting university facilities and public property and respecting the rule of law and institutional rules. Recognising that consensus does not require uniformity, they said they would work together on common interests such as environmental protection, community service, sanitation and academic development. They pledged inclusive student leadership that serves all students fairly, regardless of political affiliation or electoral support. They also committed to safeguarding academic freedom and the right to political participation, while upholding campus safety, fairness and university rules so that politics enriches teaching and learning.

items.title: Historic private estate goes on sale for £65m
items.description: A mansion once home to lieutenant-governors, a marmalade magnate and family of Oscar-winning actresses has been put on the market for £65m. Havilland Hall in Guernsey sits in about 80 acres of land, has six bedrooms, seven bathrooms, five reception rooms, an indoor pool and is being marketed as the island’s largest private estate. The property’s nearly 200-year history includes periods owned by marmalade businessman William Keiller, while descendants of its original owner included Oscar-winning actresses Olivia de Havilland and Joan Fontaine. Estate agents Savills said estates of this scale were “extraordinarily rare in the Channel Islands and it is likely to draw a global audience.” Built by Lieutenant-Colonel Thomas Fiott de Havilland between 1829 and 1830, it later served as the official residence of Guernsey’s lieutenant-governors. William Keiller, whose family created the first commercial Dundee marmalade brand, was among the estate’s former owners. The estate was bought in 1922 by Count Lothair Blücher von Wahlstatt, whose family traced its ancestry to the Prussian commander whose forces helped the Duke of Wellington defeat Napoleon at the Battle of Waterloo. The estate also has a connection to the wider de Havilland dynasty, whose later generations included aviation pioneer Sir Geoffrey de Havilland and Olivia de Havilland and Joan Fontaine. As well as the main house, the estate includes five guest cottages, staff accommodation, office space, converted farm buildings, a wine cellar and games room. Phillippa Dalby-Welsh, head of Savills’ country department, described Havilland Hall as a “pre-eminent Channel Island estate”. She said: “At its heart is a distinguished Regency villa, with great provenance, alongside beautiful gardens, a wide range of ancillary accommodation, leisure facilities and the infrastructure to support a business operation. “Estates of this scale are extraordinarily rare in the Channel Islands and it is likely to draw a global audience.” Nick Paluch, head of Savills’ Guernsey open market residential business, said: “This truly is a superb home and a once in a generation opportunity.”

items.title: AMA warns of sanctions for non-compliance with November 7 sanitation exercise
items.description: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has warned residents, traders and businesses in the metropolis that individuals found operating during the November edition of the National Sanitation Day exercise or obstructing clean-up activities will face legal sanctions. The exercise is scheduled for Saturday, November 7, 2026, from 6:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon across the Accra Metropolis. In a statement issued on , the Assembly disclosed that it had so far prosecuted 27 offenders for failing to participate in previous clean-up exercises as part of efforts to enforce sanitation regulations and promote responsible environmental practices. It stressed, however, that the exercise was not intended to generate revenue through fines and penalties but to promote behavioural change, encourage public participation and instil a culture of cleanliness among residents. The November exercise will involve sweeping streets and public spaces, desilting choked drains, clearing weeds, removing accumulated refuse and cleaning markets, lorry parks, commercial centres and residential communities. The activities will be undertaken in accordance with the AMA (Communal Labour) By-laws, 2017. The Assembly said it would deploy Environmental Health Officers, members of its Sanitation Task Force and other enforcement personnel to monitor compliance across the metropolis. Residents have consequently been urged to clean their immediate surroundings, clear weeds and drains in front of their premises, and properly gather waste for collection and evacuation. The AMA has also appealed to traditional authorities, religious leaders, market associations, transport unions, youth groups, corporate institutions and other stakeholders to mobilise their members and support the exercise. It urged residents, traders and business operators to participate actively, emphasising that maintaining a clean and healthy environment was a shared responsibility that should not be left solely to sanitation workers and local authorities. The statement was signed by the AMA Head of Public Affairs, Gilbert Nii Ankrah, on behalf of the Metropolitan Chief Executive.

items.title: No Bed Syndrome: Mahama announces expansion of accident and emergency centres at four major hospitals
items.description: President John Mahama has announced plans to expand the accident and emergency centers at four major hospitals in the country, with work expected to begin next year. The expansion will target Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, Tamale Teaching Hospital and the 37 Military Hospital as part of efforts to address pressure on their Accident and Emergency departments. President Mahama said the government is working towards increasing emergency bed capacity to at least 10 per cent of each facility’s functional bed capacity. Using Korle Bu Teaching Hospital as an example, he said the hospital has a functional bed capacity of 1,500 but only 65 beds in its Accident and Emergency Department. He explained that meeting the proposed 10 per cent target would require more than doubling the existing emergency beds. “At Korle Bu, for example, achieving this target would mean more than doubling the current emergency bed capacity from 65 to at least 150 beds,” he said. The President indicated that the expansion would not be limited to providing additional beds but would also include the necessary human and logistical resources to make them operational. “The expansion will be matched with the necessary staff, equipment, oxygen and essential supplies to make the additional capacity fully operational,” he stated. President Mahama also announced the piloting of an Integrated Bed Management and Referral Coordination System (IBMRC) through the Ministry of Health. The digital platform involves Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, Tamale Teaching Hospital, Greater Accra Regional Hospital at Ridge, 37 Military Hospital, the University of Ghana Medical Centre and the National Ambulance Service. The system is intended to help hospitals and ambulance teams identify facilities with available capacity to receive patients and coordinate their transfer. He said the effectiveness of the system would depend on accurate information about the actual clinical capacity available at each facility. Meanwhile, the Ghana Armed Forces Critical Care and Emergency Hospital is being opened to the public to provide additional capacity for managing emergency cases. President Mahama said the facility would begin receiving patients immediately, adding that closer cooperation between military and civilian health services would help make better use of the country’s available healthcare resources. He also reiterated that health facilities must not turn away patients arriving in critical condition simply because they have no available beds. “When a patient arrives in critical condition, we cannot simply say, ‘No bed, no bed, go somewhere else.’ At the very least, the patient must be assessed,” he said. He stressed that where definitive treatment is unavailable, facilities must provide stabilisation within their capacity before coordinating a safe transfer to another hospital. The President further said families must receive clear information and guidance throughout the referral process and should not be left to navigate a fragmented healthcare system on their own.

Massacre de Shakahola au Kenya: 200 ans de prison pour le meurtrier des 191 personnes
items.description: Le chef de la secte apocalyptique kényane, le pasteur Paul Mackenzie, a été condamné à la prison à vie, précisément 200 ans de prison, pour le meurtre de 191 personnes, à l’issue du jugement sur le massacre de Shakahola, ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026. Le pasteur autoproclamé de l'Eglise internationale de la Bonne Nouvelle, Paul Mackenzie, au Kenya a été condamné à 200 ans de prison, ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026 à Mombasa, pour le meurtre de 190 enfants et d'un adulte dont les corps avaient été retrouvés dans la forêt de Shakahola, dans l'Est du pays, en 2023. Ses 28 coaccusés passeront également le reste de leur vie incarcérés, a annoncé ce vendredi la Haute Cour de Mombasa. Le dirigeant de la secte apocalyptique Paul Mackenzie, qui prêchait à ses adeptes un jeûne extrême pour rejoindre Jésus, a échappé à la peine de mort comme l’avait requis le parquet en début de semaine. « Mais la juge s’y est refusée, notamment parce qu’elle estimait que, compte tenu de la doctrine de Paul Mackenzie, la mort serait sans doute perçue comme une libération », a rapporté la radio mondiale qui note pourtant que la magistrate a exposé tous les éléments qui accablaient Paul Mackenzie et ses complices. Par Wakat Séra L’article Massacre de Shakahola au Kenya: 200 ans de prison pour le meurtrier des 191 personnes est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Haho/5è Promotion de l’ENFPE: 195 futurs enseignants effectuent leur rentrée académique 2026-2028
items.description: Notsè, 6 nov. (ATOP) – L’Ecole normale de formation des professeurs d’écoles (ENFPE) de Notsè a effectué sa nouvelle année académique. La cérémonie solennelle de rentrée de la 5 è promotion, regroupant 195 élèves-professeurs dont 96 femmes, s’est déroulée le vendredi 5 novembre, en présence du préfet de Haho, colonel Gnakou Alowégnim. Le déroulement de la cérémonie a été rythmé par l’exécution de l’hymne national et normalien, la présentation des plans de formation ainsi qu’une conférence inaugurale axée sur le thème : « Le professionnalisme, l’excellence et les valeurs citoyennes, socle de compétence du professeur d’école ». Des intermèdes musicaux assurés par la chorale de l’ENFPE ont également marqué la rencontre. Le directeur de l’ENFPE de Notsè, Adanglo Kouami a indiqué que ces 195 auditeurs ont été retenus à l’issue d’un processus rigoureux de présélection. Il a précisé que le programme de formation, d’une durée de deux ans, associera harmonieusement théorie et pratique. Il a souligné que le cursus englobe plusieurs disciplines clés, notamment les langues et la communication (français, anglais, éwé et kabiyé), les sciences et technologies, les arts plastiques, la musique, l’histoire-géographie, ainsi que les sciences sociales. M. Adanglo a exhorté les nouveaux pensionnaires à s’approprier les textes régissant l’organisation et le fonctionnement de l’institution afin de garantir le succès de leur parcours. Le préfet de Haho, colonel Gnakou Alowégnim a exhorté les apprenants à la recherche constante de l’excellence, la discipline afin de servir de modèle pour les prochaines promotions. Selon lui, l’ouverture des activités de la formation des ENFPE pour le compte de la rentrée académique 2026-2028 marque la ferme adhésion à la modernisation du système éducatif dictée par le gouvernement. Il a ajouté que «la formation des enseignants est identifiée donc comme un axe stratégique pour améliorer la qualité de l’enseignement et le relèvement du niveau scolaire des apprenants». Depuis le 4 novembre 2022, les Ecoles normales d’instituteurs (ENI) ont changé de dénomination et deviennent les Ecoles normales de formation de professeurs d’écoles (ENFPE). Elles offrent désormais une formation initiale de deux ans sanctionner par le Diplômé de professeur d’école primaire (DPE) en lieu et place du Certificat de formation d’étude normale d’instituteur (CFENI). ATOP/YM/SED

items.title: Assemblée nationale : Les députés examinent le budget rectificatif 2026 et le budget 2027
items.description: Lomé, 6 nov. (ATOP) – Les députés de la commission des finances et du développement économique de l’Assemblée nationale ont entamé, le vendredi 6 novembre à Lomé, l’examen du projet de loi de finances rectificative, exercice 2026, et du projet de loi de finances initiale 2027. Les travaux ont été ouverts par le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Prof. Komi Selom Klassou. L’examen en commission porte sur les prévisions budgétaires, les échanges avec les responsables des différents départements ministériels et la répartition des ressources au regard des priorités nationales. Il se déroule conformément aux dispositions de la Constitution, de la loi organique relative aux lois de finances, du règlement intérieur de l’Assemblée nationale et des directives communautaires de l’UEMOA. Le ministre des Finances et du Budget, Essowè Georges Barcola, a expliqué que la révision du budget 2026 tient compte de la dégradation de l’environnement international et des mesures prises pour soutenir le pouvoir d’achat et améliorer les conditions de vie des populations. Le budget rectificatif est arrêté à 2 744,2 milliards de francs CFA. Le déficit budgétaire passe à 247,6 milliards, soit environ 4 % du produit intérieur brut (PIB), contre 206,6 milliards, représentant 3 % du PIB, dans la loi de finances initiale. Cette hausse est principalement liée au renforcement des mesures de soutien aux populations. Le gouvernement entend également poursuivre les investissements structurants tout en préservant la soutenabilité des finances publiques, a-t-il dit. Pour 2027, le projet de budget s’élève à 2 684,1 milliards de francs CFA en ressources et en dépenses. Le secteur social bénéficie de 48,8 % des crédits, contre 28,4 % pour la transformation de l’économie et 22,8 % pour le renforcement de l’État, qui comprend notamment le développement des territoires. Le président de l’Assemblée nationale a relevé que l’examen des deux textes intervient dans un contexte marqué par des défis économiques, sécuritaires et climatiques. Il a invité les députés à examiner les propositions en tenant compte de leur impact sur la vie quotidienne des citoyens. Il a insisté sur la nécessité d’apprécier non seulement les dépenses prévues, mais aussi les résultats attendus, notamment dans les domaines de la santé, de l’éducation, de l’emploi des jeunes et de l’accès à l’eau potable. Les ressources publiques, a-t-il souligné, doivent répondre aux besoins des populations et contribuer à un développement équitable des différentes régions du pays. Les deux projets de loi seront examinés successivement par l’Assemblée nationale et le Sénat, conformément au principe du bicaméralisme consacré par la Constitution du 6 mai 2024. ATOP/AO/BV

items.title: La campagne nationale de production du soja 2026-2027 lancée
items.description: Lomé, 6 nov. (ATOP) – La campagne de production du soja au Togo, au titre de la saison 2026-2027, a été lancée le vendredi 6 novembre à Lomé sous le thème « Soja togolais : transformer localement, financer durablement et conquérir les marchés de demain ». Organisée par le Conseil interprofessionnel de la filière soja (CIFS), cette campagne ambitionne d’accroître la production nationale, de renforcer la transformation locale et de mieux positionner le soja togolais sur les marchés internationaux. Elle met l’accent sur l’amélioration des performances de la filière et le renforcement des partenariats entre les acteurs. Des périodes d’approvisionnement ont également été définies pour permettre aux unités de transformation de disposer de matières premières en quantité suffisante. Pour le soja biologique, cette période s’étend du 6 novembre au 5 décembre, tandis que celle du soja conventionnel s’étend du 6 novembre au 31 janvier 2027. Ces délais doivent permettre aux transformateurs de constituer des stocks nécessaires à la poursuite de leurs activités. La cérémonie de lancement a été marquée par la signature d’accords interprofessionnels entre les trois principales composantes de la filière, sous la coordination du CIFS. Il s’agit de la Fédération nationale des coopératives de producteurs de soja (FNCPS), de l’Association togolaise des transformateurs de soja (ATTS) et de l’Association nationale des commerçants et exportateurs de soja (ANCES). Ces accords définissent les engagements de chaque organisation et encadrent leurs relations contractuelles pour faciliter le déroulement de la campagne. Signature des accords L’assistance Le secrétaire général du ministère en charge de l’Agriculture, Essiomle Komi, a insisté sur la nécessité de renforcer le positionnement du soja togolais face à la concurrence internationale. Il a particulièrement mis en avant la qualité du soja biologique produit au Togo. « Beaucoup de pays produisent du soja, mais le monde entier doit savoir que, lorsqu’on recherche du soja biologique de qualité, le Togo est une référence. C’est ce positionnement que nous devons davantage renforcer pour la filière », a-t-il déclaré. Le président du conseil d’administration du CIFS, Koriko Mounirou, a annoncé un objectif de production de 300 000 tonnes de graines de soja pour la campagne 2026-2027. Il a également fait état de nouveaux engagements des acteurs, notamment sur la sécurité et la qualité des produits. « Nous avons donné des consignes fermes afin que le soja acheminé soit de bonne qualité. Des innovations ont également été introduites dans la sécurisation et la disponibilité de la matière première », a-t-il expliqué. Il a, par ailleurs, indiqué que la période moratoire a été prolongée afin de donner aux unités de transformation davantage de temps pour constituer leurs stocks. ATOP/MD/AO

items.title: Hamile dynamite explosion: FOSDA calls for investigation into explosives movement, border security vulnerability
items.description: The Foundation for Security and Development in Africa (FOSDA) expresses grave concern over the dynamite explosion in Hamile, Lambussie District, in the Upper West Region, on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, which reportedly claimed the lives of a Ghana Immigration Service officer and two civilians, with several others sustaining injuries. FOSDA extends its deepest condolences to the bereaved families, the Ghana Immigration Service and all affected by this tragic incident. We also wish the injured, including the Immigration officer currently receiving specialised medical treatment in Accra, a speedy recovery. While investigations into the incident have reportedly commenced, the circumstances surrounding the explosion and the subsequent confrontation between community members and security personnel raise serious questions that go beyond the immediate tragedy. FOSDA considers the Hamile incident a matter of national security that demands urgent national attention, a comprehensive investigation and decisive preventive action. It must not be treated merely as an isolated explosives accident or a localised border security incident. A National Security Concern That Demands Urgent Attention Reports from the Ghana Immigration Service indicate that the explosives were being transported on a motor tricycle through an unauthorised route towards Burkina Faso when Immigration officers attempted to intercept the vehicle. The resulting explosion claimed the lives of the two civilian occupants and one Immigration officer. The reported movement of dynamite through an unauthorised border route raises critical fundamental questions about the acquisition, transportation, regulation and possible trafficking of explosive materials within Ghana and across its borders. Of particular concern is the possibility that this incident has exposed the movement of dangerous explosive materials through informal cross-border networks beyond the effective reach of existing regulatory and security arrangements. Although there is currently no established evidence linking this incident to terrorist activity or organised armed groups, the potential implications of uncontrolled explosives movement for national and regional security cannot be overlooked. Civilian-Security Relations and Accountability Of particular concern are accounts received by FOSDA suggesting that the explosion may have occurred after one of the Immigration officers allegedly discharged a firearm at the motorcycle in an attempt to immobilise it during the interception. If established, this raises serious questions about the operational procedures governing the interception of vehicles suspected of transporting dangerous or explosive materials, including the risks associated with the use of firearms in such circumstances. FOSDA recognises that the circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation. However, this account, alongside the reported civilian casualties during the subsequent confrontation, makes it imperative that investigators establish the precise sequence of events, including whether a firearm was discharged before the explosion, who discharged it, the circumstances under which it was used and whether established operational protocols were followed. Equally concerning are reports of a subsequent confrontation between sections of the Hamile community and security personnel, during which additional civilians reportedly sustained gunshot wounds and other injuries as a result of military intervention. Accounts from local representatives and media reports have raised questions about the circumstances surrounding the discharge of firearms and the resulting civilian casualties. These allegations must be independently established. While FOSDA recognises the difficult and often dangerous responsibilities undertaken by security personnel in protecting Ghana’s territorial integrity, security operations must be conducted in accordance with established standards of professionalism, necessity, proportionality and respect for human rights. The loss of civilian lives and injuries arising from the subsequent confrontation, if confirmed, must not be overlooked in the broader investigation. Restoring calm in Hamile is important. However, lasting security requires more than the deployment of security personnel and the imposition of curfews. It requires public confidence, accountability, community engagement and trust between security institutions and the populations they serve. FOSDA Calls for a Comprehensive Investigation FOSDA calls on the Government, through the relevant national security and law enforcement institutions, to ensure a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation into the full circumstances surrounding the incident. In particular, the investigation must establish clear answers to the following critical questions: The origin and supply chain of the explosives. The intended destination and possible end-users. The subsequent confrontation and civilian casualties. These questions must not remain unanswered. The investigation must go beyond establishing the immediate cause of the explosion to identify any wider trafficking networks, institutional gaps or systemic weaknesses that may have contributed to the incident. FOSDA’s Recommendations In light of the incident, FOSDA calls for the following measures: 1. A coordinated and comprehensive national investigation The Government should ensure effective coordination among the Ghana Police Service, Ghana Immigration Service, Ghana Armed Forces, relevant explosives regulatory institutions and national security agencies to establish the facts, identify any trafficking networks and ensure accountability. The investigative process should include an independent civilian oversight component, particularly in examining the circumstances surrounding the reported use of firearms and civilian casualties. 2. A review of explosives control and regulation Relevant authorities should undertake a comprehensive review of existing systems for the licensing, acquisition, transportation, storage and monitoring of explosives. Particular attention should be given to informal supply chains, unauthorised transportation routes and the potential diversion of explosives into illicit activities. FOSDA encourages Ghana to, as a matter of urgency, endorse the UN Declaration on the Use of Explosives in Populated Areas (EWIPA). 3. Strengthening and Empowering Border Security Committees (BOSEC) Government should prioritise the institutional strengthening, resourcing and operational empowerment of Border Security Committees (BOSEC) to enable them to effectively discharge their mandates across all border communities. This should include adequate logistical and operational resources, regular capacity-building, improved intelligence-gathering and information-sharing mechanisms. 4. Accountability and protection of civilians The reported civilian casualties arising from the subsequent confrontation must be independently investigated. Any violations of established operational procedures or human rights standards must be addressed through appropriate accountability mechanisms. 5. Strengthened community-security engagement Government and security agencies should deepen engagement with traditional authorities, local government structures, youth groups and community representatives in border communities. Communities must be treated as essential partners in identifying and preventing security threats, with accessible and trusted channels for reporting suspicious activities and raising grievances. 6. Enhanced regional cooperation Ghana should strengthen cooperation with Burkina Faso and other relevant regional partners to address the illicit movement of explosives and other dangerous materials across borders. Intelligence-sharing and coordinated border management are essential to preventing the exploitation of informal routes by illicit networks. FOSDA recognises the important role played by security personnel in protecting Ghana’s territorial integrity and maintaining peace, particularly in communities along the country’s borders. The death of an Immigration officer in the line of duty is a painful reminder of the risks faced by personnel entrusted with this responsibility. However, effective national security cannot be achieved through enforcement alone. It requires strong regulatory institutions, effective intelligence systems, accountable security operations, and the confidence and cooperation of communities. We therefore urge residents of Hamile and surrounding communities to remain calm, cooperate with lawful investigations, and refrain from acts of violence or reprisals. We further call on the Ministry of the Interior and the relevant national security institutions to provide credible public updates on the investigation, its findings and the measures being taken to address the underlying vulnerabilities. The Hamile incident must serve as a wake-up call for Ghana. The movement of dangerous explosives across our borders, the potential vulnerabilities in their regulation and the resulting loss of civilian and security personnel lives are matters that demand national attention and decisive preventive action.

items.title: The Epstein Election and the End of MAGA
items.description: This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. Sign up for it here. I n the final weeks before the midterms , the name Epstein was everywhere—in political ads, in stump speeches, on T-shirts at campaign rallies, and even in a scandal on The Real Housewives of New York City . Two years ago, invoking Epstein was a winning part of the Republican playbook. This time around, not so much. As Donald Trump ran for reelection, he told voters that his administration would release the Epstein files and filled its ranks with people who had fanned lurid interest in the case, including Kash Patel, Dan Bongino, and J. D. Vance. But then, once in office, they botched the process, turning off voters who had been essential to Trump’s movement. The president’s decision to go to war with Iran and the resulting spike in gas prices may have been the front-of-mind issues for most voters in the 2026 midterms. But members of Congress, pollsters, political operatives, and campaign staff all told me that Trump’s mishandling of the Epstein issue meaningfully contributed to the GOP’s drubbing. The Republican pollster and strategist Brent Buchanan told me that Epstein became “a proxy for corruption” in the midterms. Another Republican close to the White House described the Epstein issue to me as the “nuclear fuel” that accelerated a new form of American populism. First, it boosted Trump. But on Tuesday, it worked against him, helping bring him to the lowest point of his presidency. Many of Trump’s voters viewed his handling of the matter as a betrayal. Pollsters told me it had cracked the bond between Trump and his coalition—and changed the course of the midterms. F lorida Governor Ron DeSantis said at a news conference Wednesday that the midterm election was as “close to an extinction-level event for Republicans in many parts of the country as we have seen probably in the last 100 years.” Among the causes for catastrophe, in DeSantis’s view: The party should have voted to release the Epstein files sooner. The reluctance of Republicans in Congress, and Trump himself, to do so was the stuff of Democratic-campaign messaging throughout the fall: Candidates and super PACs spent tens of millions of dollars on Epstein-related ads. In Texas, James Talarico boasted, “I’ve never given a sweetheart deal to a pedophile.” In Georgia, Jon Ossoff’s campaign charged that his opponent had “protected powerful elites” by voting against the Epstein-files disclosure. In Ohio, Sherrod Brown accused his opponent of taking “the most money from associates of Jeffrey Epstein”; in Maine, a Democratic-aligned super-PAC ad alleged that Susan Collins had “voted with Trump to cover up the Epstein files.” [ Read: Susan Collins didn’t have a chance ] For Republicans, the impact of the “Epstein issue” in the 2026 midterms is a source of frustration and embarrassment—and was often described to me as an unforced error, especially given how the subject had first entered the political consciousness. Epstein immediately became fodder for conspiracy theorists after his death in a New York prison in 2019. In December of 2021, then–Senate candidate Vance posted a conspiratorial question to his Twitter followers: “What possible interest would the US government have in keeping Epstein’s clients secret? Oh…” In a 2023 podcast interview, the future FBI director Kash Patel asked, “What the hell are the House Republicans doing? They have the majority. You can’t get the list?” He said, “Put on your big-boy pants, and let us know who the pedophiles are.” Six months later, then-candidate Trump said in an interview that he would release the Epstein files—a stance that won him widespread praise on the right, particularly among people who don’t usually engage with politics. But that promise meant very different things to different audiences. Epstein was indicted in July 2019 for creating “a vast network of underage victims for him to sexually exploit.” He died by suicide a month later while in custody awaiting trial, leaving behind a long list of unanswered questions. Those he abused, and others who followed the case, wanted to understand who else had known about Epstein’s crimes without reporting them, and how he had escaped justice for so long. And they wanted to hold to account those who had enabled him. They expected to find answers to these questions in Epstein’s emails, his personal papers, and the investigative files of law-enforcement agencies. But others thought they already knew the answers to these questions. Victims’ allegations that Epstein had trafficked women to other powerful men led people to believe that Epstein had engaged in blackmail—and that the government was covering it all up, as Vance implied. They thought that Epstein had kept a list of such men, the so-called client list to which Patel referred. They believed that some of the world’s wealthiest and most powerful men were on that list, and that releasing the Epstein files would reveal that people at the highest levels of government were covering up for elites engaged in a secret child-abuse ring. And they suspected that anyone who declined to produce evidence to substantiate their theory was participating in that cover-up. But the idea of releasing the files, so simple in theory, became far more complicated once Trump, Vance, and Patel took office. In February 2025, Trump’s first attorney general of his second term, Pam Bondi , was asked by Fox News about the supposed Epstein client list and replied that it was “sitting on my desk right now to review.” Then the White House promised bombshells when it distributed binders labeled The Epstein Files: Phase 1 to right-wing influencers. (Nearly all of the material was redacted or already public.) In July 2025, the administration abruptly changed course with little explanation. That month, the Department of Justice and FBI released a memo saying there would be no further Epstein-related disclosures and there was no basis for further investigations or charges. The memo was unsigned, a person familiar with the memo told me, because there was no one within DOJ’s or the FBI’s senior leadership who would agree to put their name to it. The Republican political strategist and former Trump-administration official Matthew Bartlett told me that the Epstein files were, for a time at least, a rare bipartisan political issue. Republicans believed that the files would incriminate Bill Clinton and other prominent Democrats. Democrats thought the same about Trump. But some figures in the administration promised far more than they could deliver, feeding conspiracy theories that were never going to be proved. “Some of them were shameful in their statements and allegations, and then came up with nothing,” Bartlett said. “That planted the seed of distrust.” Shortly after the DOJ/FBI memo was released, the president issued a Truth Social post addressing what he called “The Jeffrey Epstein Hoax,” which he suggested was being perpetrated by Democrats. “My PAST supporters have bought into this ‘bullshit,’ hook, line, and sinker,” he wrote. Trump ended his post by declaring, “I don’t want their support anymore!”—a comment that some of his onetime supporters told pollsters and focus-group moderators only increased their suspicions. White House officials and others close to the president cite the explosion of the Epstein story last summer as the first moment that threw Trump 2.0 off its stride. Until then, his second term had been a veritable steamroller through Washington. But the chatter around the scandal—including from some Republican loyalists—rattled the White House. Later that year, Trump sought to block Congress from voting to release the files—and relented only when he realized that enough Republicans had defected to join Democrats in supporting the legislation to pass it. The Justice Department subsequently released millions of documents, but the process was hasty and error-filled, and it hasn’t quieted suspicions that the government is covering for people in high places. Lauren Bis, a White House spokesperson, told me in a statement that “President Trump has done more for Epstein’s victims than anyone before him.” Multiple Republican pollsters and operatives told me they viewed July 2025 as the first step in the unraveling of the MAGA coalition. “That is the beginning of that bond breaking,” Rich Baris, the director of Big Data Poll, told me. First it was the Epstein files, “and then you follow it up with the Iran war, and it’s just a devastating one-two punch.” [ Read: The simple message that produced a Democratic landslide ] Democrats’ invocation of Epstein—and adoption of the Epstein class as an epithet to describe their opponents—has proved an effective tactic. Over the past year, Democrats have used the term to encompass broader Republican political vulnerabilities: high prices, corruption, and a lack of trustworthiness. A review of political advertising from this cycle shows that mentions of Epstein appeared in at least 79 federal and state races across 26 states. AdImpact identified at least $76 million in spending on ads mentioning Epstein, overwhelmingly from Democrats in competitive races. AdImpact estimates that Republicans spent $3 million on Epstein-related ads as of late October, and the final weeks of Republican ad buys reflect GOP candidates trying to turn the issue around on their opponents, often pointing to Democratic donors whose names surfaced in the Epstein files. In Alaska, Senator Dan Sullivan said in a TV ad: “I voted to force Trump’s DOJ to release the Epstein files, while Mary Peltola took huge checks from Epstein’s associates.” In Georgia, during a mid-October debate, Ossoff’s opponent, Mike Collins, declared, “This call is coming from inside the house. And the Epstein class is onstage right now. And it’s you.” The National Republican Congressional Committee spokesperson Mike Marinella told me, “Americans have been disgusted by the level of self-serving corruption that spread like herpes through the slimy politicians who run the Democratic Party while getting bankrolled by Jeffrey Epstein’s best friend, megadonor Reid Hoffman. Voters see through the facade, and they know Republicans are cleaning up the rot left behind by Democrat leaders.” (Hoffman has denied knowledge of Epstein’s crimes and has called for further transparency by the government.) D emocrats have won this time , but they now face a new challenge. Once they control both the House and the Senate, they will be expected to deliver on their accountability promises despite a DOJ and FBI that have been unwilling to pursue Epstein-related investigations. A poll by Data for Progress, a left-leaning firm, found that 72 percent of voters wanted DOJ and the FBI to do more related to Epstein, though 45 percent did not believe that any Americans would actually be arrested. Representative Jamie Raskin is expected to become the chair of the House Judiciary Committee when Democrats take the majority next year. While in the minority, Raskin’s team has devoted substantial resources to Epstein-related investigations, culminating in a 52-page staff report released last week that called on DOJ to appoint an independent special counsel to conduct additional criminal investigations into Trump’s relationship with Epstein —and accused Trump’s DOJ of suppressing evidence. Raskin told me he and other Democrats plan to focus on pressuring DOJ to release the roughly 2.5 million remaining Epstein-related documents still believed to be in DOJ’s possession, as required by law, and demanding that potential crimes be investigated. (A DOJ spokesperson has said the department has released all of the documents required and that the remaining files are nonresponsive to the Epstein Files Transparency Act. The remaining files are the subject of multiple civil lawsuits.) [ Read: The Epstein emails show how the powerful talk about race ] Raskin acknowledged that with an administration that appears unwilling to respond to congressional subpoenas, there was a substantial risk of not being able to deliver on voters’ expectations, calling it both “a great responsibility” and a “very serious challenge.” California Representative Ro Khanna told me that Democrats expect those who campaigned on the Epstein issue to follow through once they’re in Congress: “The people who are winning on this issue are really going to have to be leaders on issues of sexual trafficking and assault and accountability more broadly,” he told me. Democrats on the House Oversight Committee put out a press release Tuesday night stating that, as incoming chair, Robert Garcia would take on “the Trump Crime Family, corporate corruption, DHS and ICE abuses, and the cover-up of the Epstein files.” Garcia’s own statement was only two words: “Lawyer up.” But even if Democrats secure the release of all of the remaining documents, they may face their own version of the current Republican bind. Their aggressive rhetoric is raising expectations that they may not ultimately be in a position to fulfill. And unless those documents bear out the darkest and most conspiratorial theories about Epstein, Democrats may be left trying to convince voters that they aren’t also part of the cover-up. L ast month , I met with a small group of Epstein victims and their advocates who had gathered in New York for a ceremony in which Virginia Roberts Giuffre posthumously received an award for speaking out about Epstein’s abuse. (Giuffre died by suicide in 2025.) The midterms were less than two weeks away. The women described the frequent Epstein ads and references to their abuser in stump speeches as surreal. They were candid about the personal costs of their private trauma becoming a political tool, including the therapy bills and mounting credit-card debt to cover the costs of travel to lobby members of Congress. Other victims have told me they have taken on multiple jobs or relied on donations and food banks to feed their children. Giuffre’s brother Sky Roberts told me that his sister’s experience with Epstein was ultimately the product of a political and judicial system that failed her and other victims. “It’s not political, but it is the political state that got us here today, blue and red, and there are just as many Democrats in there as there are Republicans in the files,” he told me. Roberts said he remains hopeful that both parties will continue to pursue transparency efforts to prevent future abuses. He described a meeting with Republican House Oversight Chairman James Comer that surprised him—and gave him confidence. “I remember him sitting back in the chair after listening to the survivors and to our family, and he goes, ‘I have daughters,’” Roberts recalled. “And immediately he flipped, like there was this switch.” Comer’s committee has conducted more than a dozen depositions and interviews, obtained information about Epstein’s bank accounts, referred two individuals to the DOJ for investigations, and held the Epstein associate Leon Black in contempt of Congress. The families of victims told me they never got into this to be agents of one political camp or another. “If somebody abused your daughter or your sister,” Roberts told me, “you wouldn’t ask first if he was a Democrat or a Republican.” Jonathan Lemire, Marie-Rose Sheinerman, Madison Hahamy, and Jack Rodriquez-Vars contributed reporting.

items.title: Approvisionnement en eau potable des cités religieuses : Mbacké Kadior et Daroul Mouhty bien desservies
items.description: Mbacké Kadior et Daroul Mouhty ont été desservies d’eau potable dans le cadre de la politique d’approvisionnement des cités religieuses du Sénégal. L’annonce a été faite vendredi par l’Office des Forages ruraux (OFOR) à travers un communiqué. L’Office des forages ruraux (OFOR) continue de dérouler des programmes de renouvellement, de réhabilitation et de mise à niveau les ouvrages (forages et châteaux d’eau) à Mbacké Kadior et à Daroul Mouhty, deux cités religieuses situées dans le département de Kébémer. Dans le cadre des préparatifs du Magal de Mbacké Kadior prévu le dimanche 8 novembre 2026, le Directeur général de l’Office des Forages Ruraux (OFOR) Serigne Mbacké Dieng a rendu visite au khalife de la cité religieuse Serigne Moustapha Mbacké le jeudi 5 novembre 2026. « A cet effet, il a indiqué au khalife que tous les engagements pris lors du Comité Régional de Développement (CRD) de préparation du Magal seront respectés. L’OFOR, en collaboration avec la Sénégalaise Des Eaux Rural (SDER) a pris toutes les mesures qui concourent à une couverture correcte en eau potable durant l’événement », rapporte le communiqué. En plus des deux forages qui sont fonctionnels, un dispositif d’appoint sera mis en place avec six camions citernes et autant de bâches à eau. La SDER a fait l’entretien des Systèmes d’Alimentation en Eau Potable (SAEP) et a mobilisé ses équipes d’intervention qui veillent au grain. Au nom du khalife, le porte-parole de la famille Serigne Cheikh Thioro Mbacké a magnifié l’appui constant de l’Etat à tous les niveaux particulièrement dans le domaine de l’eau avec une diligence et une réactivité constantes du Directeur général de l’OFOR et de ses équipes. Il a souligné qu’actuellement l’eau coule des robinets et aucun dysfonctionnement n’a été relevé. A lire aussi : Daroul Mouhty: sacralité de la ville, le message fort du khalife Le Maire de Mbacké Kadior, Mame Mor Sylla a également magnifié les efforts étatiques à travers l’OFOR et les actions de la SDER en vue d’améliorer la desserte en eau dans sa commune. Malgré tout, il a réitéré au Directeur Général de l’OFOR l’impérieuse nécessité de réaliser un nouveau forage afin de mieux couvrir les besoins des populations. Après Mbacké Kadior, indique le texte, le Directeur général de l’OFOR s’est rendu à Daroul Mouhty dans le département de Kébémer, où il a visité les forages F5, F3 et le chantier du nouveau château d’eau en cours de réalisation, en compagnie du responsable de l’entreprise en charge des travaux CGCOC. « Si pour F3, l’ouvrage réhabilité fonctionne normalement avec un débit de 33 m3 par heure, c’est tout à fait le contraire pour F5 à l’arrêt depuis quelques jours. Sur ce cas précis, M. Dieng a donné des instructions pour que CCPS répare le forage au plus tard cette fin de semaine (dimanche prochain) », lit-on dans le communiqué. À la suite des visites sur sites, il a rencontré le porte-parole du khalife de Daroul Mouhty, Serigne Bassirou Mbacké Abdou Khoudoss. Le guide religieux l’a vivement remercié avant de lui faire part des pannes des deux châteaux d’eau dont les vannes de sortie sont grippées. Il urge de relever que les cinq forages de la cité religieuse fonctionnent mais des interventions irrégulières sur les réseaux de distribution sont notées causant parfois des dysfonctionnements. Le Directeur général de l’OFOR a annoncé une mission très prochainement afin de faire un diagnostic et un plan d’action pour résorber les difficultés. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Bilawal urges federal govt to engage all political forces instead of ‘fighting everyone’
items.description: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Friday urged the PML-N-led federal government to engage all political and social stakeholders rather than “fighting everyone”. Responding to a query at a ceremony in Larkana, the PPP chairman highlighted that people around the world were bearing the economic burden of the US-Israeli war on Iran. “This is a backbreaking burden. We have not seen this phenomenon in the past,” the former foreign minister said, adding that even if the war ended tomorrow, its economic consequences were unlikely to end soon. Bilawal contended that regardless of whether a country was directly involved in the war or not, supporting its people had become the biggest test for many governments. “I advise the federal government that this is the time to engage with the political, social and provincial stakeholders rather than fighting everyone,” he remarked. The PPP chairman further stressed that the coalition government’s focus should be on the economic difficulties faced by the people, not on their “differences with each other”. “If the federal government and the relevant stakeholders focus on the problems faced by the people, only then we can emerge successful in this test, no matter how long it goes on for,” he said, referring to the economic consequences of the Middle East conflict. However, Bilawal cautioned that if “we continue to fight among ourselves” and keep fighting with PTI and Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman — alongside the fight against terrorists, India, Afghanistan and others — then they might end up remaining engaged in that. “Our priority should be the problems faced by the people,” he stressed. Bilawal’s remarks follow exchanges of harsh remarks in recent weeks between Fazl and federal ministers, after the JUI-F chief accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights. Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He has accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments. Meanwhile, the PTI-led opposition and the Centre have been at odds over various issues, particularly the counterterrorism policy. On Oct 16, without naming anyone, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had claimed that a “head of a party” was “extremely upset over being denied a role in the new setup in KP and not getting the governorship”. The next day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry rebuked Fazl directly, who later clarified his criticism was aimed at policies, not state institutions. The row played out in the Parliament as well, where Fazl questioned Asif’s absence and Naqvi’s presence at a meeting of the Makkah pact countries and Iran in Tehran. In his response the next day, the interior minister explained his participation and went on to assail the JUI-F for “continuously crossing the line” and accused it of “extracting wealth from the state”. Bilawal defends imposition of governor’s rule in KP In his remarks, the PPP chairman rejected the accusations that counterterrorism was a pretence to dismiss the elected PTI government in KP by imposing the emergency and governor’s rule. “This claim is not based on facts,” he asserted. “The PPP maintains that the democratically elected governments are always in a better position to deal with all matters, including terrorism,” Bilawal said. However, he noted, the recent surge in terrorist activities and the number of fatalities had never been witnessed since around 2007-2008. “After the change of the government in Afghanistan, the terrorists’ threats to Pakistan have increased. This is a ground reality,” the ex-foreign minister said. Bilawal contended that during PTI’s rule in KP, individuals imprisoned on charges of terrorism had been released. He further said Sohail Afridi — the chief minister who has been rendered non-functional due to governor’s rule — had failed to combat terrorism and protect the people of his province, thereby leaving no constitutional or legal reasons for the president to reject the summary for emergency. Thanking the federal government for engaging with the PTI on his party’s recommendation, the PPP chairman recalled the breakdown of the talks between the opposition and the government, attributing their failure to the KP CM. “Even the opposition leaders who were negotiating with us know that they cannot blame anyone, including the prime minister, for this move,” Bilawal said. “Even today, I invite the PTI to negotiate and request the government to engage with them. Do not close the door for talks,” he urged, stating that if a consensus is reached on countering terrorism, he would be the first person calling to end the governor’s rule. The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were later endorsed by the Parliament amid protests by the opposition. Electoral reforms ‘fundamental issue’ On electoral reforms, the PPP chairman termed it a “fundamental issue” and called the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER) a primary platform to address the concerns. Addressing political parties that have alleged rigging in various elections, including PTI, Bilawal maintained that the reforms committee could be the starting point to resolve such grievances. Noting that opposition leaders in both the National Assembly and Senate had been empowered by PTI founder Imran Khan to make decisions regarding dialogue, Bilawal reiterated his call for them to exercise their authority by “unconditionally” naming their representatives for the PCER. “If the opposition has some other perspective, the PPP is ready to engage with them or with the government, too,” he said, emphasising that all the political parties should become part of this committee for strengthening democracy in Pakistan. “After all the efforts, if PTI does not take part in this committee, then the people of Pakistan should not pay heed to their cries against electoral rigging,” he remarked. While reaffirming his party’s call for empowering the Parliament, the PPP chairman stressed that the opposition bore an equal responsibility in achieving this, and said it had an equal role in weakening the Parliament along with the government. “If the opposition boycotts committee proceedings, then how can it criticise that the Parliament is frail?” Bilawal added, “We have to begin from somewhere; that’s why I invite the opposition to participate in the electoral reforms committee.”

items.title: Environnement : Félix Tshisekedi à Brazzaville pour un sommet sur la protection des forêts
items.description: Le president de la Republique democratique du Congo (RDC), Felix Tshisekedi, participe ce 6 novembre a un mini-sommet consacre a l'environnement, organise a Brazzaville a l'occasion de la 40e Journee nationale de l'arbre, selon le service de presse de la presidence congolaise. Le chef de l'etat est arrive la veille dans la capitale de la Republique du Congo, a l'invitation de son homologue Denis Sassou-Nguesso. Cette rencontre marque egalement le lancement anticipe de la Decennie des Nations unies pour le boisement et le reboisement (2027-2036). Reunissant plusieurs dirigeants, elle est consacree a la preservation des forets, a la restauration des ecosystemes degrades et a la gestion durable des ressources naturelles. Selon la presidence de la RDC, la participation de Felix Tshisekedi « vient consolider l'engagement du pays dans la lutte contre le changement climatique et la protection de la biodiversite, ainsi que son role strategique au sein du bassin du Congo, deuxieme massif forestier tropical au monde ». « Il s'agit ici de concilier la preservation de notre patrimoine forestier avec l'exploitation de la foret comme instrument de chauffage et d'alimentation. En Republique democratique du Congo, c'est l'agriculture itinerante sur brûlis ainsi que l'exploitation du bois-energie qui sont les moteurs de la deforestation. Il faut attaquer ces deux problemes de maniere frontale et simultanee », a declare le president congolais lors du sommet. Le mini-sommet de Brazzaville se tient a quelques jours de la 31e Conference des Nations unies sur les changements climatiques (COP31), prevue du 9 au 20 novembre a Antalya, en Turquie. a cette occasion, le Programme des Nations unies pour l'environnement (PNUE) participera a plus de 130 evenements consacres aux solutions scientifiques et aux partenariats pour concretiser les engagements climatiques.
